# Managers and datasources

A **manager** finds dependencies in files and edits them. It records byte spans, and an update replaces only those bytes, so files are never reformatted. A **datasource** lists the available versions of a dep.

Every discovered file goes to every manager whose file pattern matches. Discovery always prunes `.git`, `node_modules`, `vendor` and `testdata`, plus anything matched by [`ignorePaths`](configuration.md#ignorepaths).

The tables give the dep types (for [`rules[].depTypes`](configuration.md#rulesdeptypes)) and skip reasons. Skip reasons are exact strings, shown by `deps plan --show-skipped` as `skip    <file>:<line>  <name>  <reason>`.

## Skip reasons of every manager

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `ignored by rule #<i>` | a pre-policy rule set `ignore: true` |
| `ignored by default (<type>; enable with a rule setting ignore: false)` | dep types `indirect`, `test-indirect`, `go`, `peerDependencies`, `engines`, `submodule`, `task` |
| `non-version value "<v>"` | the current value is not valid in the dep's versioning scheme |
| `non-version tag` | a docker-datasource dep with a non-version tag (`latest`, `bookworm`, a commit hash), not pinned, and `pin: keep` |
| `current version <v> not found upstream (pin an existing version)` | a pinned or to-be-pinned dep whose current tag or image tag no longer exists (digest refresh and pin need it) |

## github-actions

Finds `uses:` references to actions and reusable workflows in GitHub, Gitea and Forgejo workflow and action files, the version inputs of known setup actions, and GitHub-hosted runner labels in `runs-on:`.

**Files:**

- `(workflow-templates|.github|.gitea|.forgejo)/(workflows|actions)/**/*.y(a)ml`
- any `action.y(a)ml`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `uses: owner/repo[/path]@ref` | `git-tags` | `tag` | updated |
| `setup` | the version input of a setup action (see Setup action inputs) | per action (see Setup action inputs) | `semver` or `tag` | updated |
| `github-runner` | a GitHub-hosted runner label in a job's `runs-on:` (`ubuntu-24.04`, `macos-15`, `windows-2025`; see Runner labels) | `github-runners` | `docker` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `local action` | `./…`, `$/…` |
| `docker reference (docker manager)` | `docker://…`, handled by the docker manager |
| `unrecognized uses` | no `@`, missing owner/repo/ref, unparsable URL |
| `non-version ref` | a branch or other ref that is not a tag (`@main`) |
| `pinned without version comment` | a SHA followed by a comment that is no version (`# main`) |
| `cannot locate value` | the value's bytes could not be found on its line |
| `expression` | setup input: `${{ … }}` |
| `non-version value` | setup input: empty or a word such as `lts/*`, `stable` |
| `unsupported range` | setup input: a range rather than a literal version |
| `non-version value` | runner label: `<runner>-latest` (`ubuntu-latest`) |

**Extracted.**

- every scalar `uses:` outside `with:` and `env:`. This covers steps, job-level reusable workflows, `parallel:` and composite `runs.steps`.
- `owner/repo[/path]@ref` uses the [default host](configuration.md#actionsdefaulthost). `https://host/owner/repo@ref` names its host explicitly.
- The dep name is `owner/repo[/path]`. The source is `https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>`.

**Ref forms.**

- Tag: `@v4`, `@v4.2.0`.
- Pinned: `@<40/64-hex sha> # v4.2.0`, or `# ratchet:owner/repo@v4`.
- Commit pin: a bare `@<40/64-hex sha>` without a comment (see Commit pins).
- An action in a subdirectory (`owner/repo/<path>`) may carry a per-action tag prefix, `<path>/` or `<last path element>/`, in the tag or the comment: `@get-vault-secrets/v1.3.1`, `@<sha> # get-vault-secrets/v1.3.1`.
- Anything else is skipped.

**Commit pins.**

- A bare SHA that a tag points at is that tag's version (the newest one: `v4.2.0` rather than a floating `v4` on the same commit). It is updated like a pinned ref, and the new version is written as a comment: `@<sha>` → `@<new sha> # v4.3.0`. Rules match it with that version.
- A bare SHA no tag points at is ignored by default (`ignored by default (commit pin without version; …)`), as Renovate disables such unversioned references. A rule setting `ignore: false` (e.g. `managers: [github-actions]`, `names: [owner/repo]`) enables a `digest` update to the commit of the repository's default branch (its `HEAD`, listed with the tags in the same request), without a comment. The `digest` update type's `allowedUpdateTypes`, schedule and `minimumReleaseAge` (against the commit date, looked up only when a minimum applies) apply.
- Actions of the repository itself are not special-cased: once enabled, each new commit on its default branch is a new digest.
- Security advisories are not looked up for bare SHAs.

**Monorepo tags.**

- An action in a subdirectory of a repository that tags each action (`grafana/shared-workflows/actions/get-vault-secrets` with tags `get-vault-secrets/v1.3.1`) is versioned by the tags prefixed `<path>/` or `<last path element>/`; the version after the prefix is compared and written, digests and release times are looked up by the prefixed tag.
- Without such tags the repository's tags are the versions. A rule's `extractVersion` replaces this.

**Replacements.**

`uses: owner/repo[/path]@ref` can be [replaced](configuration.md#rulesreplacementname) by another `owner/repo[/path]` on the same host. A per-action tag prefix in the ref or the pinned version comment is rewritten in the same form (full path or last element); a one-element prefix moving to a multi-element path is rejected as ambiguous.

**Edits.**

- A tag is replaced by the new tag at the same precision (`@v4` → `@v5`, `@v4.1.0` → `@v4.2.0`).
- A pinned ref gets the new SHA, and the comment version is replaced.
- With `pin: digest`, a tag becomes `@<sha> # <tag>`.
- A floating pin (`@<sha> # v4`) whose tag moved gets a digest refresh.
- A per-action tag prefix is kept: `@get-vault-secrets/v1.3.1` → `@get-vault-secrets/v1.4.0`, pinned as `@<sha> # get-vault-secrets/v1.4.0`.
- A `with: version:` input equal to the current version (the tag or the pinned comment version) is bumped in the same edit, e.g. `@<sha> # v0.2.5` with `version: v0.2.5`. A different value is left alone, and setup actions keep their own version input (DepType `setup`).

**Setup action inputs.**

For these actions, the version input in `with:` is also a dep (DepType `setup`):

| Action | Input | Datasource | Name |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actions/setup-go` | `go-version` | `go-toolchain` | `go` |
| `actions/setup-node` | `node-version` | `node-version` | `node` |
| `azure/setup-helm` | `version` | `github-releases` | `helm/helm` |
| `azure/setup-kubectl` | `version` | `github-releases` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` |
| `golangci/golangci-lint-action` | `version` | `github-releases` | `golangci/golangci-lint` |
| `hashicorp/setup-terraform` | `terraform_version` | `github-releases` | `hashicorp/terraform` |

- Only literal values are extracted.
- A full `[v]X.Y.Z` uses `semver` and keeps the `v` style.
- A partial `26`, `1.27` or `v2.1` uses `tag` versioning, and its precision is kept (`26` → `27`).
- setup-python and setup-java are not extracted.
- Skips: `expression` (`${{ … }}`), `non-version value` (empty or a word such as `lts/*`, `stable`), `unsupported range`, `cannot locate value`.

**Runner labels.**

- A job's `runs-on:` label, or each label of a `runs-on:` list, of the form `<runner>-<version>` is a dep named `<runner>` (`ubuntu`, `macos`, `windows`, `xcode`) with that version, when the table of the `github-runners` datasource (see [Datasources](#datasources)) lists the version: `ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `macos-15-large`, `windows-11-arm`. `<runner>-latest` is skipped. Other labels (`self-hosted`, larger-runner names, `${{ … }}` expressions, `runs-on: {group: …}`) are not deps, as in Renovate.
- Updates keep the suffix: `ubuntu-22.04` → `ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-22.04-arm` → `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `macos-14-large` → `macos-15-large`. Deprecated images are never targets; a dep on one gets a `deprecated` warning.
- Only the version is rewritten; runner labels are never digest-pinned.
- Workflows under `.gitea/` and `.forgejo/` are skipped: their runners advertise labels of their own configuration (act_runner's `ubuntu-22.04` maps to an image the runner chose), so GitHub's images would be the wrong update source. Renovate extracts them too.

## gomod

Updates the requirements and the `go`/`toolchain` directives of Go modules, and the `go`/`toolchain` directives of Go workspaces. `go.mod` and `go.work` are parsed with `golang.org/x/mod/modfile`.

**Files:**

- `go.mod`
- `go.work`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `direct` | `require` without `// indirect` | `go` | `go` | updated |
| `indirect` | `require … // indirect` | `go` | `go` | ignored (opt in with a rule setting `ignore: false`) |
| `go` | `go 1.x` directive of `go.mod` or `go.work` | `go-toolchain` | `tag` | ignored (opt in with a rule setting `ignore: false`) |
| `toolchain` | `toolchain go1.x.y` of `go.mod` or `go.work`; the span covers the version after `go` | `go-toolchain` | `tag` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `replaced` | a `replace` directive targets the module |
| `prerelease toolchain` | `go1.27rc1` style directive |
| `cannot locate value` | the version bytes were not found |
| `module path changed to <path> (<module>@<version>)` | every newer candidate's `go.mod` declares another module path (a renamed module, or a fork that kept its origin's path); go refuses such a version |

**Versioning.**

- `go` versioning excludes pseudo-versions, prereleases (unless the current version is one), `+incompatible` (unless the current version has it), and other majors (except v0 → v1).
- Directives move at their precision: `go 1.26` → `go 1.27`, `go 1.26.1` → `go 1.27.1`.

**Pseudo-versions (digest updates).**

- A requirement on a pseudo-version (`v0.0.0-<timestamp>-<commit>`) tracks a commit. A newer release (above the pseudo-version's base, e.g. `v1.2.4` for `v1.2.4-0.<ts>-<commit>`) is proposed as a version update; prereleases only when the base is one.
- Otherwise the module's `@latest` is asked: when it is a newer pseudo-version of the same major (the tip of the default branch of an untagged module), it is proposed as a `digest` update, titled `update <module> digest to <commit7>`.
- Rules apply as for other digest updates (`allowedUpdateTypes: [digest]`, `ignore`, `updateTypes: [digest]`); `minimumReleaseAge` of the digest type is checked against the commit time.
- Modules with releases whose pseudo-version is ahead of the latest release get no digest update (`@latest` is that release, not the branch tip).

**Major module paths (`gomodUpdateImportPaths`).**

- Major versions ≥ 2 live under their own module path. For a requirement on `<path>/v<N>` (or an unsuffixed v0/v1 module, `/v<M+1>` for `vM.x.y+incompatible`, `gopkg.in/x.v<N>`), deps lists `/v<N+1>`, `/v<N+2>`, … from the GOPROXY URLs until one has no releases (at most 5).
- The newest stable release of each path that the major policy accepts (`allowedUpdateTypes`, `allow`, `minimumReleaseAge`, `ignore` per update type) is a `major` update in the major PR bucket (`v<N>` buckets with `separateMultipleMajor`); a newer path replaces an older one in the same bucket.
- The update rewrites the require (path and version) and every import of the old path and its packages in the module's `.go` files (below the go.mod, skipping `vendor`, `testdata`, `.`/`_` directories and nested modules; only the import path literals change). `go mod tidy` then sees the rewritten files through `-overlay`.
- The new major's API may have changed: the PR body says so, and the build is not guaranteed to pass.
- `gomodUpdateImportPaths: false` turns module path updates off. Only GOPROXY URLs are probed: GONOPROXY/GOPRIVATE modules, and paths no proxy before `direct` has, get no module path updates.
- A probe only decides whether a module path update is offered, so each probe request to a proxy gets 10 s, retries included, and is not retried once that runs out. A path no proxy answers in time counts as having no releases and is logged as a warning (`major module path probe timed out; assuming no newer major`); the requirement keeps its other updates.

**Module path changes.**

- A version is only an update when its `go.mod` declares the path it is required as. The `@v/<version>.mod` of a candidate that passed the other checks is read from the module download cache, else the GOPROXY URLs (one request per module@version and run). One that declares another path (`github.com/google/cel-go` v0.32.0 declares `cel.dev/cel-go`) is rejected like a too new one, and the next candidate of its PR bucket is tried; for a renamed module the next 8 are fetched concurrently. This applies to major module paths and pseudo-version heads too.
- A requirement left without updates this way is skipped with `module path changed to <declared> (<module>@<version>)` (the newest such version): moving to the new path is a code change deps does not make. A failed `.mod` lookup is logged and leaves the candidate to `go mod tidy`; GONOPROXY/GOPRIVATE modules are not checked.
- When `go mod tidy` still refuses a module version this way (`module declares its path as … but was required as …`, for a module the update pulls in, or one the check could not read), `run` skips the update with the same reason instead of failing: its PR group is reported as `skipped: update cannot be applied` and is no error, so it does not keep obsolete PRs open (`apply` leaves the update out and applies the others).

**Replacements.**

A require can be [replaced](configuration.md#rulesreplacementname) by another module path; like a major module path update, the import paths in the module's `.go` files are rewritten.

**Post-processing (`apply`, `run`).**

- After any gomod change, deps runs `go mod tidy -modfile=<tmp>/go.mod` in the module directory, on temporary copies of `go.mod` and `go.sum`, with `GOWORK=off` and `GOFLAGS` cleared; source files rewritten by a major module path update are passed with `-overlay`.
- The tidied `go.mod` and `go.sum` replace the patched files. The real files are only written by `apply`.
- A module with `vendor/modules.txt` is vendored again after tidy: `go mod vendor -modfile=<tmp>/go.mod -o <tmp>/vendor` (same environment and overlay). Only the vendor files whose content changed, appeared or disappeared become part of the change (`vendor/modules.txt` and the vendored packages); the rest of the vendor tree is compared, never rewritten.
- Go workspaces: a module listed in the `use` directives of the nearest `go.work` at or above it is still tidied on its own with `GOWORK=off`, since `go mod tidy` ignores the workspace. deps does not run `go work sync`: it would raise the requirements of the other workspace modules to the workspace's build list, a change to modules the update does not touch; the updated module's own `go.sum` gets the new checksums, so `go.work.sum` needs none.
- When `vendor/modules.txt` exists next to that `go.work`, the workspace vendors its modules: the patched modules of one workspace are post-processed together (one PR group's changes in one run), each tidied as above, then `go work vendor -o <tmp>/vendor` runs in the workspace directory with `GOWORK` set to its `go.work` and the tidied `go.mod`/`go.sum` files and rewritten sources as `-overlay`. Changed workspace vendor files are part of the change as above.
- A `go.work` change (its `go`/`toolchain` directive) runs no go command.
- At most 4 post-processors (tidy and npm installs together) run concurrently.
- A failure drops that module's change: `go mod tidy in <dir>: <last 20 lines of stderr>`, `go mod vendor in <dir>: …` or `go work vendor in <dir>: …` (except a module path change, below). In a vendoring workspace this drops the changes of all its modules in the group.
- `plan` does not run tidy, and prints `note    go.sum changes are computed by apply/run`.

**Lock file maintenance (`run`).**

Go has no lockfile, and Renovate has no gomod lock file maintenance. With [lockFileMaintenance](configuration.md#lockfilemaintenance) enabled, deps treats the `// indirect` requirements (which it does not update by default) as the locked versions of each scanned `go.mod` that has a `go.sum` and is not a module of a vendoring workspace. In the module directory, on temporary copies of `go.mod` and `go.sum` and with the environment of `go mod tidy` above, deps runs `go get -modfile=<tmp>/go.mod <module>@upgrade …` for every indirect requirement without a `replace` directive, then `go mod tidy`. `@upgrade` is the newest non-retracted release of the same module path (a prerelease only when there is no release); a current version newer than that (a prerelease or pseudo-version) stays.

- The `go` and `toolchain` directives and the direct requirements do not move. When the `go get` call would move them, or go reports a version conflict between the requested modules or a module that needs a newer go than the running one, the modules are split in halves and each half is tried on the result of the one before. Only a module whose upgrade conflicts on its own keeps its version; without conflicts this is one `go get` call.
- The PR changes `go.mod` (indirect lines only), `go.sum` and, for a module with `vendor/modules.txt`, the changed vendor files (`go mod vendor` as above), and shares `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance` with the other lockfiles; `minimumReleaseAge` does not apply to it. A module with nothing to move gets no change.
- Other `go get` failures drop that module's maintenance: `go get in <dir>: <last 20 lines of stderr>`.
- With `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`, a module that needs a newer go than the running one makes go download that toolchain before deps rejects the upgrade.

## docker

Updates container image references in Dockerfiles, Compose files, workflows, actions, Kubernetes manifests and Helm values.

**Files:**

- `Dockerfile`, `Containerfile`, `Dockerfile.<x>`, `<x>.Dockerfile` (DepType `dockerfile`)
- Compose files (DepType `compose`): `compose.y(a)ml`, `docker-compose.y(a)ml`, overrides and variants (`compose.override.yml`, `compose.<env>.yaml`, `docker-compose.<env>.yml`, `<x>.compose.y(a)ml`), and any other YAML shaped like one (see Compose details)
- workflow YAML, as for github-actions (DepType `workflow`)
- `action.y(a)ml` (DepType `action`)
- other `*.y(a)ml` containing `image:` (DepType `kubernetes`) or `repository:` (DepType `helm`)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dockerfile` | `FROM` (flags skipped, line continuations and `# escape=` honored), `COPY --from=<image>`, `RUN --mount=…,from=<image>` | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `compose` | `services.*.image` (also through `<<:` merges and aliases), `image` in mappings at any depth of top-level `x-*` extension fields, `services.*.build.additional_contexts` entries `docker-image://<ref>` | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `workflow` | `jobs.*.container` (string or `.image`), `jobs.*.services.*.image`, `uses: docker://…` | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `action` | `runs.image: docker://…` (with `runs.using: docker`), `uses: docker://…` in `runs.steps` | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes` | scalar `image` in `containers`, `initContainers` and `ephemeralContainers` items (not items with a `container` key: Azure Pipelines container resources, see azure-pipelines) | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `helm` | `*image` mappings with `repository` + `tag` (optional `registry`, digest in `tag: x@sha256:…` or sibling `digest:`) | `docker` | `docker` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `variable reference` | `$` in the reference, or a variable ARG default (Compose: see `interpolated image`) |
| `interpolated image` | Compose interpolation other than `${VAR:-default}` / `${VAR-default}`, or a version spanning a variable boundary |
| `template value` | `{{` in Kubernetes or Helm values |
| `invalid reference` | the reference does not parse |
| `no tag` | the reference has neither tag nor digest |
| `digest without tag` | the reference has a digest but no tag |
| `unparsable compose file` | a Compose file name whose content is not valid YAML (e.g. an indented fragment); one dep-less skip at line 1 |
| `cannot locate value` | the value's bytes could not be found |

**Dockerfile details.**

- `scratch`, earlier stage names (`AS <name>`) and numeric stage indexes are not deps.
- A reference that is exactly `$X` or `${X}` resolves to `ARG X=<image>`, declared before the first `FROM` or in the current stage. The dep sits at the ARG default, so the update rewrites the ARG line.

**Compose details.**

- A YAML file with another name is a Compose file when every top-level key is a Compose key (`version`, `name`, `include`, `services`, `networks`, `volumes`, `configs`, `secrets`, `models`) or an `x-*` extension, and `services` is a mapping of mappings, at least one with `image` or `build`. Kubernetes manifests, workflows and Helm values fail this check.
- Anchored values are extracted once, at the anchor definition: services merging `<<: *runner` share the `x-runner` dep; a service that sets its own `image` after the merge is its own dep.
- Interpolation: `${VAR:-default}` and `${VAR-default}` resolve to the default, and the update rewrites the default bytes (`${REGISTRY:-docker.io}/nginx:${TAG:-1.27}` → `${TAG:-1.28}`). `$$` is a literal `$`.
- `build.args` values are not images. Dockerfiles referenced by `build.dockerfile` are found by the Dockerfile rules on their own.
- `include:` and `extends:` need no handling: the referenced files are scanned like every other file.

**YAML files.**

Other YAML is parsed document by document. A parse error (typically a Helm template) yields no deps and no error.

**Names.**

References are parsed as docker does (names without a registry are on docker.io, single-component ones under library/). The dep name is the familiar name (`postgres`, `ghcr.io/org/img`); lookups use the canonical name.

**Versioning.**

`docker`. Candidates need the same prefix, the same number of numeric parts and the same suffix.

**Non-version tags.**

Non-version tags (`latest`, `bookworm`, commit hashes such as `3a22eba`) only get digest maintenance: a pinned ref → `digest` refresh; unpinned with `pin: digest` → `pin`; otherwise skipped as `non-version tag`.

**Replacements.**

Image references written as one token (Dockerfiles, compose, workflows, Kubernetes manifests) and Helm values images (`repository`, and `registry` when set: the new name is split at its registry) can be [replaced](configuration.md#rulesreplacementname) by another image name; the tag and a pinned digest (of the new image) are written with it.

**Edits.**

- The tag is replaced in place.
- `tag@sha256:…` is refreshed together with the tag.
- With `pin: digest`, `@sha256:<digest>` is appended. For multi-platform images this is the index digest.

## npm

Updates dependencies, tool versions and engines in `package.json`, and the lockfile along with them or on its own (lockfile-only updates, lock file maintenance). `package.json` is stream-parsed; each value's byte span must equal the quoted value in the file, otherwise (for example with `\u` escapes) the dep is skipped as `cannot locate value`. `overrides`, `resolutions` and `bundleDependencies` are not extracted.

**Files:**

- `package.json`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dependencies` | `dependencies` (updates use commit type `fix`) | `npm` | `semver` | updated |
| `devDependencies` | `devDependencies` | `npm` | `semver` | updated |
| `optionalDependencies` | `optionalDependencies` | `npm` | `semver` | updated |
| `peerDependencies` | `peerDependencies` | `npm` | `semver` | ignored (opt in with a rule setting `ignore: false`) |
| `packageManager` | `"packageManager": "npm@x"`, `pnpm@x`, `yarn@x`; the name is the tool | `npm` | `semver` | updated |
| `engines` | `engines.{node,npm,pnpm,yarn}` | node: `node-version`; others: `npm` | `semver`; partial versions `tag` | ignored (opt in with a rule setting `ignore: false`) |
| `volta` | `volta.{node,npm,pnpm,yarn}` | node: `node-version`; others: `npm` | `semver`; partial versions `tag` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `npm alias` | `npm:` |
| `local dependency` | `file:`, `link:`, `workspace:`, `./`, `../`, `/`, `~/` |
| `git dependency` | `github:`, `gitlab:`, `bitbucket:`, `gist:`, `git+…`, `git://`, `git@`, `owner/repo[#ref]` |
| `url dependency` | `http(s)://` tarballs |
| `tag` | dist-tags such as `latest`, `next` |
| `unsupported range` | anything outside npm's range grammar (below), a range without a version (`*`, `x`), empty; for packageManager anything but a full version |
| `packageManager with hash` | `pnpm@9.0.0+sha512…` |
| `unsupported packageManager` | a tool other than npm, pnpm or yarn |
| `cannot locate value` | escaped value |

**Ranges.**

- Accepted: npm's range grammar: `||` alternatives of space-separated comparators (an optional `^`, `~`, `~>`, `>=`, `>`, `<=`, `<` or `=`, spaces allowed after it) or hyphen ranges (`1.2.3 - 2.0.0`), on partial versions with `x`, `X` or `*` wildcards and an optional `v` (`1.x`, `^1.2`, `v1.2.3`, `>=1.2.3 <2`, `^1.0.0 || ^2.0.0`). The dep's version is that of a `^`, `~`, `>=` or `=` range, else the lowest version of the last alternative's first lower bound (`^1.2` → 1.2.0, `1.x` → 1.0.0), else of its upper bound (`<2` → 2.0.0).
- How a range moves is [`rangeStrategy`](configuration.md#rangestrategy): by default (`auto` = `update-lockfile`) a version the range admits only moves the locked version, and a version outside it replaces the range (`^5.2.8` → `^6.0.0`); `bump` raises the range for every update (`^1.2.3` → `^1.4.0`), `in-range-only` only for versions it admits; `replace` leaves admitted versions alone; `widen` widens the range for the others (`^1.2.3` → `^1.2.3 || ^2.0.0`, `>=1.2.3 <2` → `>=1.2.3 <4`, an exact version is replaced); `pin` writes the exact version (`^1.2.3` → `1.4.0`): first a `pin` update to the locked version (else the newest one the range admits), unless another update shares its PR bucket, then every newer version. `auto` is `widen` for peerDependencies and for a range with `||`, as in Renovate.
- Rewrites keep each version's precision, wildcards and `v`, and the bytes between comparators: a lower bound takes the new version (`1.x` → `2.x`, `^1.2` → `^2.0`, `>` becomes `>=`), an upper bound the new version reaches moves to the next compatibility boundary above it (`<2.0.0` → `<4.0.0` for 3.1.0) or, for `<=`, to the new version; a hyphen range moves its high end to a version above it and its low end to an admitted one. An admitted version raises the first alternative admitting it (`^1.0.0 || ^2.0.0` → `^1.0.0 || ^2.5.0`); outside the range, `replace` keeps only the replaced last alternative (`^1.0.0 || ^2.0.0` → `^3.1.0`). A range the new version cannot raise (`1.x` with 1.5.0) is not rewritten for it. packageManager always replaces its version; for engines and volta see below.
- For `engines` and `volta`, a full version with an optional `^`, `~`, `>=` or `=` keeps its operator and only its version is replaced (`>=26.1.0` → `>=27.0.0`), as is a partial `^26` or `10.2`, with `tag` versioning on the numeric part (`^26` → `^27`). Any other range of the grammar (`>= 22 <27`, `^24.15.0 || ^26.13.0`, `22.x`, `18 - 22`) is a range as in the dependency sections, moved under `rangeStrategy`: by default a version it admits is left alone (the lockfile does not lock tools) and one outside it replaces it (`>= 22 <27` → `>= 28 <29` for 28.1.0), while `||` ranges widen (`^24.15.0 || ^26.13.0` → `^24.15.0 || ^26.13.0 || ^28.1.0`), as in Renovate. `*`, `x` and dist-tags (`latest`) stay skipped.
- Versioning is `semver`. Prerelease candidates are only considered from a prerelease, and deprecated versions are dropped.

**Workspaces.**

A dep naming a member of the manifest's own workspace is never updated.

**Replacements.**

Dependency-section entries can be [replaced](configuration.md#rulesreplacementname) by another package: the key is renamed and the range keeps its operator for the new version; the lockfile is regenerated as for other manifest changes.

**Locked versions.**

Before resolving, deps reads the lock root's lockfile (the one the post-processor would update, see below) once per run and keeps only the entries of the extracted deps:

- `package-lock.json` and `npm-shrinkwrap.json` (`lockfileVersion` 2 or 3), streamed: the `packages` entries, where a member's own `<member>/node_modules/<name>` wins over the hoisted `node_modules/<name>`; links are not versions. `lockfileVersion` 1: the top-level `dependencies` entries.
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` (lockfile versions 5.x to 9): the `importers` entry of the manifest's directory (`.` for the root; the top-level sections of a single-project lockfile before version 9), without the peer suffix (`18.3.1(react@18.3.1)`, 5.x `_react@…`). Only each YAML document's head up to its `packages:` is parsed; pnpm 11 and later write `packageManager` and `configDependencies` into a document of their own first.
- `yarn.lock`, classic and berry: the entry whose header lists the descriptor `<name>@<range>` (berry `<name>@npm:<range>`), with the range as package.json writes it. Descriptors are shared by the whole workspace.
- `bun.lock` (text; trailing commas allowed): the `packages` entry `<member name>/<name>`, else the hoisted `<name>`; its first element is `<name>@<version>`.
- `link:`, `workspace:`, `file:`, git and alias resolutions are not versions: such deps count as not locked.
- The locked version is the current version under `update-lockfile` (update types compare it with the new version) and is what OSV is queried with, so an already locked fix is not proposed again. Without a lock, the version in package.json is used.
- A lockfile that does not parse is a run error (`<path>: <err>`); its deps are bumped under `update-lockfile` and `auto`, and OSV checks the version in package.json. So is a `package-lock.json` without `lockfileVersion`. `bun.lockb` (bun's binary lockfile) is not a lockfile to deps.

**Lockfile post-processing (`apply`, `run`).**

1. **Lock root.** The lock root is the nearest directory at or above the `package.json` (within `--dir`) that holds `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock` or `bun.lock`. It is accepted if it is the manifest's own directory, or if its `package.json` `workspaces` (an array or `{packages}`) or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `packages` globs match the manifest directory (`!glob` excludes). Otherwise the manifest is only patched; no lockfile is created.
2. **Temporary copy.** The root and all member `package.json` files (patched where changed), the lockfile, `.npmrc`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `.yarnrc.yml`, `bunfig.toml`, and the files referenced by `yarnPath`/`plugins` are copied to a temp dir. So are the local files the install resolves: yarn `patch:` files (from `package.json` and `yarn.lock`), pnpm `patchedDependencies` files (`package.json` `pnpm` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml`), the pnpmfile (`.pnpmfile.cjs`, or the `pnpmfile` setting), and the targets of `file:`, `link:` and `portal:` dependencies, resolutions and overrides (a tarball itself, a directory's `package.json` only). Such files may lie above the lock root within the repository (the nearest directory with `.git`), at their relative paths; paths outside it are not copied. npm 12 no longer reads or writes `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, so it is copied as `package-lock.json` (the same format) and the result is written back under its own name.
3. **Install.**

   | Tool | Command |
   |---|---|
   | npm | `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` |
   | pnpm | `pnpm install --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts --no-frozen-lockfile` |
   | yarn berry (`.yarnrc.yml`, or `__metadata` in the lock) | `yarn install --mode=update-lockfile`, with `YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS=0 YARN_ENABLE_IMMUTABLE_INSTALLS=0` |
   | yarn classic | `yarn install --ignore-scripts --ignore-engines --non-interactive --no-progress` |
   | bun | `bun install --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts` |

   The environment always includes `npm_config_update_notifier=false` and `COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0`.
4. **Tool lookup.** deps uses the tool binary from `PATH`. Failing that:
   - if the root's `packageManager` names the tool, `npx --yes <tool>@<version>` (for yarn berry, `npx --yes --package=@yarnpkg/cli-dist@<version> -- yarn`);
   - else `npx --yes <tool>`;
   - else error `<tool> not found (needed to update <lock>)`.
5. **Several lockfiles.** If a root has more than one lockfile, the `packageManager` tool's lockfile wins, else `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, then `bun.lock`.
6. **Lockfile-only updates.** The manifests stay unchanged: only the lockfile is read back from the copy. The plain install runs first only when a manifest of the root changed (yarn classic and bun install from the pinned manifests instead). Then, per tool:

   | Tool | Commands |
   |---|---|
   | npm | `npm install … <name>@<version>` for the root manifest's updates, `npm install … --workspace=<dir> <name>@<version>` per workspace member; npm saves `^<version>` into the lockfile's own package entries (`packages[""]`, `packages["<member dir>"]`), and deps restores the range package.json holds, so `npm ci` accepts the lockfile (a missing entry is an error). A v1 lockfile comes back as npm writes it (version 3). |
   | pnpm | `pnpm update --no-save --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts --filter <sel> <name>@<version>…` per manifest (`<sel>` is `.` for the root, `./<dir>` for a member); the specifiers stay. |
   | yarn berry | `yarn set resolution <name>@npm:<range> npm:<version>` per descriptor. |
   | yarn classic | an install from manifests whose updated ranges are replaced by the new versions, which adds `<name>@<version>` entries; deps moves each `<name>@<range>` descriptor into that entry (out of its old one, which goes away when nothing is left), then installs from the real manifests, which drops the pinned descriptors nothing else uses. |
   | bun | an install from manifests pinned the same way; deps puts the ranges package.json holds back into `bun.lock`'s `workspaces` entries. |

   Every tool locks exactly `<version>`. In yarn, a descriptor is shared by every manifest and dependency that requests the same `<name>@<range>`, so they all move.
7. **Failure.** A failed command reports `<tool> <subcommand> in <dir>: <last 20 output lines>` (e.g. `pnpm update in …`), and the root's changes are dropped.

- `plan` does not run installs, and prints `note    package-lock.json changes are computed by apply/run`; lockfile-only updates are listed as `(<type>, lockfile)` without a diff.

**Lock file maintenance (`run`).**

With [lockFileMaintenance](configuration.md#lockfilemaintenance) enabled, the lockfile of every lock root of a scanned `package.json` (the one picked as above; a root without its own `package.json` is skipped) is regenerated from scratch in the temporary copy, as Renovate does: `package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `bun.lock` are left out and `yarn.lock` is copied empty (so yarn keeps the directory as its project root), then the install command above runs (npm twice, since its first lockfile can be out of sync with `package.json`). Every locked package, direct and transitive, of the root and all workspace members moves to the newest version its range admits; the `package.json` files are unchanged, and the lockfile's own root and workspace entries keep their ranges. The tool lookup (`packageManager` version, `npx`) is the same as above. All lockfiles share the PR on `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance`, which changes only lockfiles; `minimumReleaseAge` does not apply to it.

## helm

Updates Helm chart versions in Chart.yaml dependencies (with Chart.lock), Helm v2 requirements.yaml (with requirements.lock), helmfiles and chart custom resources, from classic chart repositories and OCI registries.

**Files:**

- `Chart.yaml` (DepType `chart`)
- `requirements.y(a)ml` of Helm v2 (`apiVersion: v1`) charts (DepType `requirements`); files without `dependencies` (Ansible Galaxy) yield nothing
- `helmfile.y(a)ml`, `helmfile.d/*.y(a)ml`, each optionally `.gotmpl` (DepType `helmfile`)
- other `*.y(a)ml` containing the API group of a k0s, Flux, Argo CD or Sveltos resource below, parsed document by document (DepTypes `k0s`, `flux`, `argocd`, `sveltos`)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chart` | `dependencies[].version` with `name` and `repository` | `helm` | `semver` | updated |
| `requirements` | `dependencies[].version` with `name` and `repository`, as in Chart.yaml | `helm` | `semver` | updated |
| `helmfile` | `releases[].version` with `chart: <repo>/<name>` (resolved through `repositories[]`, `oci: true` → `oci://`) or `chart: oci://host/path/name` | `helm` | `semver` | updated |
| `k0s` | k0s `Chart` (`helm.k0sproject.io`) `spec.chartName` + `spec.version`, and ClusterConfig (`k0s.k0sproject.io`, also embedded in a k0sctl `Cluster` as `spec.k0s.config`) `spec.extensions.helm.charts[].chartname` + `version`; the repository is `spec.repository.url`, the `<alias>` of `<alias>/<chart>` from a ClusterConfig's `spec.extensions.helm.repositories[]` in any file, or `oci://host/path/<chart>` | `helm` | `semver` | updated |
| `flux` | `HelmRelease` (`helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v2*`) `spec.chart.spec.chart` + `version` from its `sourceRef` `HelmRepository` (`source.toolkit.fluxcd.io`, any file; `spec.type: oci` → `oci://`), and the `OCIRepository` chart (`spec.url` + `spec.ref.tag`) a `spec.chartRef` names or whose `spec.layerSelector.mediaType` is the Helm chart type | `helm` | `semver` | updated |
| `argocd` | `Application` `spec.source` / `spec.sources[]` and `ApplicationSet` `spec.template.spec.source(s)` with a `chart`: `repoURL` + `chart` + `targetRevision`; a `repoURL` without scheme is an OCI registry | `helm` | `semver` | updated |
| `sveltos` | `ClusterProfile` and `Profile` (`config.projectsveltos.io`) `spec.helmCharts[]`, `ClusterPromotion` `spec.profileSpec.helmCharts[]` and `EventTrigger` (`lib.projectsveltos.io`) `spec.helmCharts[]`: `chartVersion` of `chartName` (without its `<repositoryName>/` prefix) in `repositoryURL`; an `oci://` `repositoryURL` is the chart reference itself | `helm` | `semver` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `version range` | anything but a full `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-pre][+build]` (optionally `v`-prefixed): `~1.2.0`, `^1`, `>=1.0.0`, `1.2.x`, `1.2` |
| `no version` | the version is missing or empty |
| `template value` | the version (or a resource's chart name, `repoURL` or `repositoryURL`) contains `{{` |
| `local chart` | Chart.yaml, requirements.yaml: empty or `file://` repository; helmfile: a chart path (`./x`, `../x`, `/x`, no `/`); k0s: a chart path (`/x`, `./x`, `*.tgz`) |
| `repository alias` | Chart.yaml, requirements.yaml: `@name` or `alias:name` repositories (resolved by the user's Helm repository config) |
| `unknown chart repository <repo>` | Chart.yaml: a repository that is no URL; helmfile: a `<repo>/` prefix not in `repositories[]`; k0s: an alias no scanned ClusterConfig declares |
| `ambiguous chart repository <alias>` | k0s: ClusterConfigs in other files declare the alias with different URLs (the chart's own file declares none) |
| `invalid chart reference` | helmfile and k0s: `oci://` without a path, or `<repo>/a/b`; k0s: a chart name without `/` |
| `unknown HelmRepository <namespace>/<name>` | flux: no scanned HelmRepository matches the `sourceRef` |
| `ambiguous HelmRepository <name>` | flux: the `sourceRef` matches HelmRepositories with different URLs |
| `chart from <kind> source` | flux: the `sourceRef` is a `GitRepository` or `Bucket` |
| `no sourceRef` | flux: the HelmRelease chart has no `sourceRef` kind |
| `pinned by digest` | flux: the OCIRepository selects `spec.ref.digest` |
| `no repoURL` | argocd: a Helm source without `repoURL` |
| `no repositoryURL` | sveltos: a `helmCharts[]` entry without `repositoryURL` |
| `cannot locate value` | the version's bytes could not be found (escapes, block scalars) |

**Versioning.**

`semver`: the `v` prefix style of the current value is kept, prereleases are only proposed from a prerelease. Only exact versions are updated; Helm treats everything else as a constraint.

**Chart.lock and requirements.lock.**

- After Chart.yaml is patched (`plan`, `apply`, `run`), the sibling `Chart.lock` gets the new version of every exact dependency whose locked version differs, matched by position and name.
- `digest` is recomputed as Helm does (`sha256` over the JSON of the Chart.yaml and Chart.lock dependencies), so `helm dependency build` accepts the lock. Repository aliases take the URL locked for them.
- The old digest is verified first; when deps cannot reproduce it (a lock out of sync), the chart's update fails with an error instead of writing a lock Helm would reject.
- A Helm v2 `requirements.yaml` is handled the same way with its sibling `requirements.lock`; its digest is either Helm 2's (`sha256` over the JSON of the requirements alone, aliases as written or resolved) or Helm 3's (as for Chart.lock), whichever reproduces the old digest, and the new digest uses the same.
- `generated` is kept, so unchanged updates produce identical commits.

**Kubernetes resources.**

- Repository references are resolved across files once every file was extracted: a k0s alias from any ClusterConfig (its own file first), a HelmRelease `sourceRef` by namespace and name (the namespace defaults to the HelmRelease's). When one side has no namespace (a Kustomization sets it), the name alone must match a single URL.
- A Flux `OCIRepository` (`spec.ref.semver` skips as `version range`) that neither a HelmRelease `chartRef` names nor declares the Helm chart media type is a Kustomization artifact, not a dep.
- HelmReleases with a `chartRef` carry no version; the OCIRepository does. Container images in the same files (values) are found by the docker manager.

**Replacements.**

A chart is [replaced](configuration.md#rulesreplacementname) by a chart name (same repository), or `<http(s):// or oci:// URL>/<chart>` (or `host/path/<chart>` for OCI) to move it, where the repository is written next to the chart (Chart.yaml `repository`, Argo CD `repoURL`, Sveltos `repositoryURL`, Flux OCIRepository `url`, k0s `url`, `oci://` references); alias and `sourceRef` repositories only allow a new chart name, and Sveltos `oci://` charts, named in both `repositoryURL` and `chartName`, none. `Chart.lock` entries follow the renamed or moved chart.

**Edits.**

The version is replaced in place.

## kustomize

Updates image tags and digests, Helm chart versions and the `?ref=` of remote git resources in Kustomize kustomization files.

**Files:**

- `kustomization.yaml`, `kustomization.yml`, `Kustomization`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `images[]` `newTag` (`1.2` or `1.2@sha256:…`) and `digest` of `newName`, else `name` | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `helmChart` | `helmCharts[]` `version` of chart `name` from `repo` (`https://`, `http://` or `oci://`) | `helm` | `semver` | updated |
| `resource` | remote git targets in `resources[]`, `components[]` and `bases[]` with a `ref` (or `version`) query parameter: `[git::]https://host/org/repo[.git][//path]`, `ssh://[user@]host/…`, `git@host:org/repo[.git][//path]`, `host/org/repo[//path]`; the span covers the ref value | `git-tags` | `tag` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `no tag` | image: no `newTag` and no `digest` (a rename only) |
| `digest without tag` | image: a `digest` without `newTag` |
| `invalid reference` | image: the name and tag are no valid image reference |
| `invalid digest` | image: a `digest` field that is not `sha256:…` |
| `variable reference` | image: the name or tag contains `$` |
| `no repo` | helmChart: no `repo` (a chart from `chartHome`) |
| `unknown chart repository <repo>` | helmChart: a `repo` that is no `https://`, `http://` or `oci://` URL |
| `no version` | helmChart: the version is missing or empty |
| `version range` | helmChart: anything but a full `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-pre][+build]` (optionally `v`-prefixed) |
| `no ref` | resource: an empty `ref=` |
| `commit ref` | resource: the ref is a full commit SHA |
| `non-version ref` | resource: the ref is a branch or a tag that is no `v?N[.N[.N]]` version |
| `invalid repository URL` | resource: no repository path could be derived from the target |
| `cannot locate value` | the value's bytes could not be found (escapes, block scalars) |

**Remote resources.**

- Without `//`, the repository ends at `.git`, after `_git/<repo>` (Azure DevOps), after `org/repo` on github.com, gitlab.com and bitbucket.org, or at the end of the path.
- The dep name is `host/org/repo`; tags are listed from `https://host/org/repo` (also for `ssh://` and scp-like targets). Targets without a `ref` track a branch and are no deps.

**Replacements.**

An `images` entry is [replaced](configuration.md#rulesreplacementname) by rewriting its `newName`, or by inserting `newName: <image>` after `name` (which the manifests match on); flow-style entries are not replaced. A `helmCharts` entry takes a chart name, or `<repository URL>/<chart>` to move it, which also rewrites `repo`.

**Edits.**

The tag, chart version or ref is replaced in place; a digest-pinned image also gets its new digest. Images without a digest are not pinned: kustomize would need a new `digest` field.

## pre-commit

Updates the `rev` of the hook repositories in pre-commit configurations, plain tags and SHAs frozen by `pre-commit autoupdate --freeze`.

**Files:**

- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.pre-commit-config.yml` at any depth

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `repository` | `repos[]` entry with `repo` and `rev`; the name is the URL path (`owner/repo`), the source its `https://` URL without `.git` | `git-tags` | `tag` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `local repository` | `repo: local` |
| `meta repository` | `repo: meta` |
| `unrecognized repo` | `repo` is not an https/http/ssh/git or `git@host:path` URL with an owner/repo path |
| `no rev` | the entry has no `rev` |
| `pinned without version comment` | `rev` is a 40-hex SHA without a `# frozen: <version>` (or `# <version>`) comment |
| `non-version ref` | `rev` is neither a SHA nor a version tag |
| `cannot locate value` | the rev bytes were not found (block scalars) |

**Edits.**

- Tag revs are replaced in place, keeping quotes and comments.
- Frozen revs get the new SHA and the version in the `# frozen:` comment is rewritten.
- Pinning a tag rev writes the SHA and inserts ` # frozen: <version>` after the value.

## gitlabci

Updates container images, project includes and CI/CD components in GitLab CI configuration. Covers both Renovate managers `gitlabci` and `gitlabci-include`.

**Files:**

- `.gitlab-ci.y(a)ml`, `<x>.gitlab-ci.y(a)ml`
- `*.y(a)ml` under `.gitlab/ci/`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `image` (string or `name:`) at top level, in `default` and in jobs | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `service` | `services[]` entries (string or `name:`) at top level, in `default` and in jobs | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `include` | `include` entries with `project` + `ref` (single mapping or list); Source `<instance URL>/<project>` | `git-tags` | `tag` | updated |
| `component` | `include` entries `component: <host>/<project>/<name>@<version>`; Source `<instance URL>/<project>` when `<host>` is the instance host or `$CI_SERVER_FQDN`/`$CI_SERVER_HOST`, else `https://<host>/<project>` | `git-tags` | `tag` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `variable reference` | `$` in the image, project, component or ref, other than a leading `$CI_SERVER_FQDN`/`$CI_SERVER_HOST` in a component |
| `no ref` | a project include without `ref` (default branch) |
| `no version` | a component without `@<version>` |
| `invalid component` | a component path with fewer than three segments |
| `non-version ref` | a branch or `~latest` instead of a version tag |
| `invalid reference` | the image reference does not parse |
| `no tag` | an image without tag |
| `digest without tag` | an image pinned by digest only |
| `cannot locate value` | the value bytes were not found (escapes, block scalars) |

**Details.**

- Images are parsed and edited like the docker manager: tags update, digests are refreshed or pinned.
- String includes and `local`, `remote` and `template` includes are not deps.
- The instance URL is `gitlabci.url` from the config, else `CI_SERVER_URL` (set by GitLab CI), else the GitLab platform `deps run` detected from the remote, else `https://gitlab.com`; a path prefix such as `https://example.com/gitlab` is kept.
- A leading `$CI_SERVER_FQDN`, `${CI_SERVER_FQDN}`, `$CI_SERVER_HOST` or `${CI_SERVER_HOST}` in a component path is the instance host; the dep name keeps the variable as written.
- Private instances authenticate with `DEPS_GITLAB_TOKEN`, or `CI_JOB_TOKEN` when running in GitLab CI against the same instance.
- Every YAML document is scanned, so component templates with a `spec:` header work.

## nvm

Updates the Node.js version in `.nvmrc`: the first token of the first line that is neither blank nor a `#` comment.

**Files:**

- any `.nvmrc`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node` | the Node.js version (name `node`) | `node-version` | `semver`; partial versions `tag` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `non-version value` | empty or a word or alias such as `lts/*`, `lts/iron`, `node`, `stable`, `system` |
| `unsupported range` | anything else that is not `[v]X[.Y[.Z]]`, such as `>=20` or `20.x` |

**Versions.**

- A full `[v]X.Y.Z[-pre]` uses `semver`, and the update keeps the `v` style.
- A partial `20` or `v20.11` uses `tag` versioning and keeps its precision (`20` → `22`); a leading `v` stays outside the replaced token.
- Only the version token is replaced; comments and the rest of the file are kept.

## asdf

Updates `<tool> <version> [fallback versions…]` lines of `.tool-versions`. Only the first version of a line is a dep; `#` starts a comment.

**Files:**

- any `.tool-versions`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tool` | a tool line; the dep name comes from the tool table | per tool (see Tools) | `semver`, `tag` or `maven` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unsupported tool` | a tool that is not in the tool table (or, for mise, an unsupported backend) |
| `non-version value` | empty or a word such as `latest`, `system`, `lts` |
| `git ref` | `ref:…` |
| `local path` | `path:…` |
| `unsupported range` | `prefix:…` or anything else that is not a version |
| `partial version` | `X` or `X.Y` for a tool whose datasource lists only full versions (github-releases, npm; `X` for go) |

**Versions.**

- A full `[v]X.Y.Z[-pre]` uses `semver`, and the update keeps the `v` style; go-toolchain tools use `tag`, `ruby` uses `ruby` (as in `.ruby-version`), `python` uses `pep440` (as in `.python-version`).
