## cargo

Updates crate requirements in `Cargo.toml`, moves `Cargo.lock` with `cargo update` (in-range updates only touch the lock, as Renovate's `update-lockfile`), and groups the crates of well-known Rust monorepos. `Cargo.toml` is read with the span-keeping TOML parser `internal/tomlspan`; only the requirement's bytes are rewritten, so comments, formatting, operators and precision are kept. `[features]` and `[package]` are not extracted.

**Files:**

- `Cargo.toml`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dependencies` | `[dependencies]` and `[target.<cfg>.dependencies]`: `name = "1.2"`, `name = { version = "1.2", features = [...] }`, `name.version = "1.2"` and `[<table>.name]` tables; `package = "<crate>"` renames are looked up by the crate name (updates use commit type `fix`) | `crate` (crates.io, or the `registry`/`registry-index` of the entry); `git` + `tag`: `git-tags` | `cargo`; git tags `tag` | updated |
| `dev-dependencies` | `[dev-dependencies]` (also `dev_dependencies`) and `[target.<cfg>.dev-dependencies]` | `crate` (crates.io, or the `registry`/`registry-index` of the entry); `git` + `tag`: `git-tags` | `cargo`; git tags `tag` | updated |
| `build-dependencies` | `[build-dependencies]` (also `build_dependencies`) and `[target.<cfg>.build-dependencies]` | `crate` (crates.io, or the `registry`/`registry-index` of the entry); `git` + `tag`: `git-tags` | `cargo`; git tags `tag` | updated |
| `workspace.dependencies` | `[workspace.dependencies]`, inherited by members with `name.workspace = true` | `crate` (crates.io, or the `registry`/`registry-index` of the entry); `git` + `tag`: `git-tags` | `cargo`; git tags `tag` | updated |
| `patch` | every `[patch.<source>]` table (`[patch.crates-io]`, `[patch."https://…"]`): versioned and git-tag entries; path patches are skipped | `crate` (crates.io, or the `registry`/`registry-index` of the entry); `git` + `tag`: `git-tags` | `cargo`; git tags `tag` | updated |
| `replace` | `[replace]`: the git tag of `"<name>:<version>" = { git = …, tag = … }` (the key's version is the package being replaced and stays) | `git-tags` | `tag` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `workspace dependency` | `workspace = true`: the requirement is inherited from `[workspace.dependencies]`, which is updated instead |
| `path dependency` | `path = ...`, also together with `version` |
| `git dependency` | `git = ...` without `tag`, with `branch`/`rev` only, or with a non-`http(s)` URL |
| `unknown registry <name>` | `registry = "<name>"` without `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_INDEX` or a `[registries.<name>] index` in the config files (Cargo cannot resolve it either) |
| `no version` | a table without `version` |
| `unsupported requirement` | anything outside Cargo's grammar: `~>1`, `1.2 - 2.0`, `v1`, `>=1.*`, empty |
| `cannot locate value` | an escaped string |
| `no Cargo.lock version for a requirement without a floor` | `*`, `<2` or `<=1.5` (nothing to raise) without a Cargo.lock entry of the crate |

**Requirements.**

- Cargo's grammar: comparators `^`, `~`, `=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` (optionally followed by spaces) or none on `MAJOR[.MINOR[.PATCH[-pre][+build]]]`, wildcards `*`, `1.*`, `1.2.x`, and comma-separated lists (`">= 0.10, < 0.11"`). A bare `1.2` is `^1.2`; `Dep.Constraint` carries that translation for the engine.
- The version a bump raises is that of the first lower bound (`^`, `~`, `=`, `>`, `>=`, none, or a wildcard's prefix). When the requirement is rewritten, every lower bound takes the new version at the precision it was written with, upper bounds `<B` that the new version reaches move to the next compatibility boundary above it, `<=B` to the new version: `1.2` → `1.4` or `2.0`, `~2.7.0` → `~2.9.1`, `1.*` → `2.*`, `">= 0.6.8, < 0.7"` → `">= 0.7.1, < 0.8"`, `<2` → `<3`.
- `rangeStrategy` (top level or per rule, default `auto` = `update-lockfile`, as in Renovate): versions the requirement admits are lockfile-only updates from the version Cargo.lock locks (`, lockfile` in the report; the manifest is unchanged); newer ones rewrite the requirement. With `bump` every newer version rewrites it, with `in-range-only` only those it admits. Without a Cargo.lock, `update-lockfile` proposes only versions outside the requirement. `replace` leaves admitted versions alone; `widen` also does and keeps the lower bounds, moving only the upper ones (`">=1.2, <2"` → `">=1.2, <4"` for 3.1.0) or, when there are none, writing `>=<lower bound>, <boundary above the new version>` (`1.2` → `">=1.2, <3"` for 2.0.1; `=1.2.3` is replaced); `pin` writes `=<version>`: a `pin` update to the locked version (else the newest admitted one) unless another update shares its PR bucket, then every newer version.
- A requirement without a floor (`*`, `<2`) has nothing to raise: its current version is the locked one, and under `bump` too its in-range updates only move the lock.
- Versioning `cargo` follows Cargo's compatibility rules: leaving the range of the leftmost non-zero part is `major` (`1.x` → `2.0`, `0.4` → `0.5`, `0.0.3` → `0.0.4`); within it a minor change of a `1.x` version is `minor`, everything else `patch`. `separateMultipleMajor` buckets are named after that range (`v0.5`). Partial requirements are compared at their precision against the release lines the `crate` datasource derives. Prereleases are only proposed from a prerelease, yanked versions never.

**Registries.**

- `registry = "<name>"` looks the crate up in that registry: the index from `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_INDEX`, else `[registries.<name>] index` of the `.cargo/config.toml` (or legacy `.cargo/config`) files from the manifest directory up to `--dir`, nearest first, then `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml` (`~/.cargo`). `registry = "crates-io"` is crates.io.
- `registry-index = "<url>"` names the index directly. `sparse+https://…` indexes are read over HTTP; any other URL is a git index, read from a shallow blob-less `git clone` (removed when the run ends) with `git cat-file`.
- The token of a registry is `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN`, else `[registries.<name>] token` of `$CARGO_HOME/credentials.toml`, else of the config files; it is sent as `Authorization`, as Cargo does, and only to the index host (a `config.json` `api` on another host gets no credentials). Without a token, the platform token is sent to its own host as Basic auth, and after a 401 the git credential helper's credentials for the index host. Git indexes use git's credential helpers.
- `[source.crates-io] replace-with` is followed (also through chains) to a mirror with `registry = "…"`; `directory`/`local-registry` replacements vendor crates.io, which stays the lookup.
- OSV advisories are only looked up for crates.io crates.

**git dependencies.**

`name = { git = "https://host/path", tag = "v1.2.0" }` (also in `[patch]` and `[replace]`) updates the tag from the repository's tags (`tag` versioning, so the prefix and number of parts are kept). The URL's query, fragment, trailing slash and `.git` suffix are dropped for the lookup.

**Lockfile (`apply`, `run`).**

1. **Workspace root.** The root is the nearest directory at or above the `Cargo.toml` (within `--dir`) that holds `Cargo.lock`. It is accepted if it is the manifest's own directory, or if its `[workspace]` `members` globs include the manifest directory and `exclude` does not. Otherwise the manifest has no lock: it is only patched, and `update-lockfile` proposes only versions outside the requirement.
2. **Locked versions.** Before resolution the root's Cargo.lock is read: each requirement gets the highest registry package of its crate that it admits. An unreadable lock is reported once and its requirements are bumped.
3. **Temporary copy.** The root is mirrored to a temp dir: every `Cargo.toml` is copied (patched where changed) together with `Cargo.lock`; all other files are symlinked, and `.git`, `target` and `node_modules` are left out. When the root sits below the repository top (the nearest ancestor with `.git`), the directories above it are recreated with their other entries symlinked, so path dependencies outside the root (`path = "../crates/x"`) resolve as in the checkout.
4. **Update.** `cargo update --workspace` re-resolves only the requirements that no longer match the lock. Then, for every rewritten requirement whose version is full, deps runs `cargo update --package <name>@<locked> --precise <version>` when Cargo just locked a newer version of the same compatibility range, so the lock holds the version the pull request names (for example when `minimumReleaseAge` held back the newest release). A version that was already locked is never downgraded, and partial requirements keep Cargo's newest match. A rewritten requirement that still admits the locked version (`<0.10` → `<2.0` with 0.9.0 locked) leaves the lock alone under `cargo update --workspace`; such a crate (also for a security update) is resolved once with its requirement written as `=<new>` in the temporary copy, then the rewritten requirement is restored and resolved again, so the lock holds the pull request's version while other dependents that still need the old version keep it locked beside it. A lockfile-only update runs `cargo update --package <name>@<from> --precise <new>`, from the entry earlier pins left in the locked version's compatibility range (pinning a crate can move its dependencies), and is skipped when that entry already has the version.
5. **Tool.** `cargo` must be on `PATH` (with `rustup`, a `rust-toolchain.toml` in the root selects the toolchain). Without it the manifests of the root fail with `cargo not found (needed to update Cargo.lock)`.
6. **Failure.** A failed command reports `cargo update in <dir>: <last 20 output lines>`, and the root's changes are dropped.

- `plan` does not run cargo, and prints `note    Cargo.lock changes are computed by apply/run`.

**Lock file maintenance (`run`).**

With [lockFileMaintenance](configuration.md#lockfilemaintenance) enabled, every `Cargo.lock` of a scanned `Cargo.toml` (its workspace root, as above) is refreshed with `cargo update` in the temporary copy, which moves every locked crate to the newest version its requirement admits. All lockfiles share the PR on `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance`, which changes only `Cargo.lock` files; `minimumReleaseAge` does not apply to it.

## pip_requirements

Updates the PEP 508 requirements of pip requirements files, and of the input files pip-compile and `uv pip compile` output files are compiled from (see Compiled files). Lines ending in `\` are joined and comments are dropped. Option lines (`-r`, `-c`, `-e`, `--extra-index-url`, `--find-links`, …) yield no deps; included files are scanned when their own name matches. An `--index-url`/`-i` line anywhere in the file becomes the index of every requirement in it, and every `--extra-index-url` line an extra index whose releases are merged in (see the `pypi` datasource). A requirements file has no lockfile: under `auto` and `update-lockfile` only versions outside a requirement's range are proposed (Renovate's `replace`); the requirements of a compiled file's inputs have its pins as lockfile. Requirements with `--hash` options are updated too: in a file that is not a compiled file deps can re-run, the `--hash` options of each updated requirement are replaced by the sha256 digests of the new version's files on its index, one option per digest in pip-compile's order and line style. `plan` shows the version changes only.

**Files:**

- `requirements.txt`, `requirements-dev.txt`, `requirements.dev.txt`, `dev-requirements.txt`, `requirements.pip` (Renovate's `(^|/)[\w-]*requirements([-.]\w+)?\.(txt|pip)$`)
- `*.in` pip-compile inputs, only when a compiled file names them (directly or through `-r`); other `.in` files (`MANIFEST.in`, `Makefile.in`) yield no deps

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `requirements` | every requirement line (`name[extras] specifier ; marker`) of a requirements file or a compiled file's input; a compiled file whose inputs deps does not read keeps its pins as `requirements` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `indirect` | a pin of a compiled file that none of its inputs names (a transitive dependency, Renovate's pip-compile `indirect`); ignored by default, but security updates still apply (rules can ignore them) | `pypi` | `pep440` | ignored (opt in with a rule setting `ignore: false`) |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unconstrained` | no specifier, `*`, or only `!=` exclusions |
| `unsupported range` | a specifier that does not parse: a version that is not PEP 440 (`>=1.0-SNAPSHOT`, `===foobar`), a wildcard other than a trailing `.*` of `==` or `!=` (`~=1.*`, `>=1.*`), Poetry syntax (`^1.2`, `>=1 <2`, `\|\|`), or a bare version outside Pipfiles |
| `cannot locate value` | a TOML string with escapes |
| `git dependency` | `git+…`, `hg+…`, `svn+…`, `bzr+…` lines or `name @ git+…` |
| `url dependency` | a URL line or `name @ https://…` |
| `local dependency` | a local path, archive or wheel (`./pkg`, `/abs`, `x.whl`, `x.tar.gz`, `file:`) |
| `conflicts with the inputs of <file> (<name>==<version>, …)` | `apply`/`run`: regenerating a compiled file fails with a resolution conflict (a pin of the inputs, or another requirement's constraint, does not admit the version); `run` reports the PR group as `skipped: update cannot be applied`, `apply` leaves the update out |

**Compiled files.**

- A compiled file is a requirements file with a pip-compile (`# This file is autogenerated by pip-compile` … `#    pip-compile <args>`) or uv (`# This file was autogenerated by uv via the following command:` / `#    uv pip compile <args>`) header. Its command is parsed shell-style and runs in the file's directory minus the `--output-file` path's directory; its inputs are the positional arguments (pip-compile without any: `requirements.in`, or `setup.py` when present).
- When every input, and every file they include with `-r`, is a requirements file deps reads (`*.in` or a `requirements*.txt`) in the compiled file's directory or below, the deps come from the inputs, as Renovate's pip-compile manager extracts them: each input requirement is a `requirements` dep with the version its compiled files pin as locked version (the lowest, when several compiled files share the input), and the compiled file keeps only the pins no input names, as `indirect`. One package yields one dep per file.
- An update of an input requirement rewrites it in the input (an `==` pin, or a range that does not admit the new version, per `rangeStrategy`) and its pin in every compiled file regenerated from that input; a version the range admits is a lockfile-only update: the input is unchanged and only the pins move (`--upgrade-package`, as npm and cargo's `update-lockfile`). `apply`/`run` then regenerate those compiled files (see Post-processing).
- An `indirect` pin is updated in its compiled file when a rule sets `ignore: false` for it, or by a security update (Renovate's vulnerability alerts force-enable pip-compile's indirect deps): the pin moves with `--upgrade-package <name>==<fix>` while the inputs stay unchanged. Lock file maintenance (`lockFileMaintenance`) re-runs each compiled file's command with `--upgrade`, which moves every pin to the newest version the inputs admit.
- Not handled as compiled from their inputs (all pins stay `requirements` deps of the compiled file, updated there and regenerated, as before): compiled files whose inputs include `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, a directory, a URL or a file deps does not read (`base.txt`), whose inputs are outside its directory, and compiled files sharing an input with such a file or with one whose command runs in another directory. A `-c` constraints file is copied for the re-run but its requirements are not deps of the compiled file.
- An input requirement without specifier (`flask`) is skipped as `unconstrained`, as in the other Python managers; its pin moves only with lock file maintenance.

**Post-processing (`apply`, `run`).**

- A compiled file whose pins changed (by its own updates or those of its inputs) is regenerated by re-running the command of its header in a temporary copy with the patched inputs and `--upgrade-package <name>==<version>` per changed pin, when the header's input files exist. pip-compile runs from PATH, else through `uvx --from pip-tools`; a header naming its Python version (`autogenerated by pip-compile with Python 3.12`) runs `uvx --python 3.12 --from pip-tools pip-compile` first, since the result depends on the interpreter and pins without wheels for another one fail to build. The header up to the command line is kept byte for byte.
- When the resolver finds that the inputs do not admit the new versions (pip's `ResolutionImpossible`, uv's `No solution found`), the update is skipped with `conflicts with the inputs of <file> (…)`: `run` skips its PR group instead of failing, `apply` leaves that update out and applies the others.

**Specifiers.**

- Every PEP 440 specifier set is accepted: `==`, `===`, `~=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` clauses separated by commas, with a trailing `.*` after `==` or `!=` (in a Pipfile also a bare version, meaning `==`). How a range is updated is described under Ranges.
- The dep's version is the range's anchor: in its last `||` alternative the first clause that is not `<`, `<=` or `!=` (`>=1.2,<2` → `1.2`, `<1.0.0,>=0.114.2` → `0.114.2`), else its first upper bound (`<2` → `2`). The anchor's precision is kept: candidates with non-zero parts beyond it are skipped (`precision`), others are cut to it (`>=1.2,<2` sees 3.1.0 as `3.1`). With a lockfile, the locked version takes the anchor's place.
- Versioning is `pep440`: pre and dev releases are only considered from a pre or dev release.
- Names are kept as written; the datasource looks them up PEP 503-normalized.

**Ranges (`rangeStrategy`).**

- `auto` (the default) is `update-lockfile`: a new version the range admits only moves the lockfile from the locked version (see Locked versions), and is not proposed without a lockfile deps reads; a version outside the range rewrites the range. Renovate's `auto` is `update-lockfile` for poetry and `replace` for pep621, pipenv and pip_requirements, which only differs where deps reads a lockfile.
- `bump` rewrites the range for every newer version, raising its lower bound (`>=1.2,<2` with 1.5.0 → `>=1.5.0,<2`, `^2.31` with 2.32.3 → `^2.32`, `>=2.31.0` → `>=2.32.3`). An admitted version a range has no bound to raise for (`<2`, `<=2`, `>1`, `==1.*`) is handled as under `update-lockfile`. `in-range-only` is `bump` without the versions outside the range.
- `replace` leaves admitted versions alone. `widen` does too, and for a version outside the range moves only its upper bounds (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=1.2,<4`); when that is not enough a Poetry constraint gets a new `||` alternative (`^2.13.0` → `^2.13.0 || ^3.0.0`) and any other range, like an exact version, is replaced. `pin` writes `==<version>` (an exact clause keeps its operator: `===1.4` → `===1.5.0`, Poetry `1.0` → `1.1`): a `pin` update to the locked version (else the newest version the range admits) unless another update shares its PR bucket, then every newer version.
- Rewrites follow Renovate's pep440 `getNewValue` (`lib/modules/versioning/pep440/range.ts`): an admitted version gets its `bump` rules, any other its `replace` rules (`widen` and `pin` aside, above), under every strategy (Renovate's `bump` would write the full new version as lower bound there too). Clause by clause: `!=` exclusions are kept verbatim; `<V` moves past the new version at the range's precision (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=3.1,<4`; with two clauses the precision is the first part in which the bounds differ, one finer for a major followed by `0`: `>=1.2.0,<2.0.0` with 3.1.4 → `>=3.1.4,<3.2.0`); `>=` and `>` take the new version at their own precision (`>=1.2` → `>=3.1`, a new version at or below them `>=<new>`); trailing zeros are trimmed when a clause has fewer than three parts; `~=`, `^` and `~` take the new version cut or zero-padded to their precision (`~=7.2` with 8.0.1 → `~=8.0`); `==`, `===`, `=`, a bare version and `<=` become the new version; wildcards keep `.*` at their precision (`==1.0.*` → `==1.2.*`).
- A Poetry constraint with `||` alternatives gets a new alternative for a version outside all of them (`^1 || ^2` with 3.0.0 → `^1 || ^2 || ^3`, as Renovate widens npm `||` ranges); `bump` raises the alternative that admits the version.
- Only the changed versions (and operators, `>` → `>=`) are rewritten; the bytes between clauses are kept. A rewrite that would not admit the new version (it is excluded by `!=`) is not proposed. Renovate's removal of a `>=` that a `==X.*` makes redundant is not done.

## pep621

Updates the PEP 508 requirement strings of `pyproject.toml` (PEP 621 project metadata, PEP 735 dependency groups, uv's and pdm's dev dependencies), then refreshes `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock` or `pdm.lock`. The file is parsed with byte spans; only the specifier's versions inside the TOML string are rewritten. `include-group` entries, `[build-system] requires` and uv's `constraint-dependencies`/`override-dependencies` are not extracted; `[project] requires-python` is no dep but drops the releases that do not support all of it (see the `pypi` datasource).

**Files:**

- `pyproject.toml`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project.dependencies` | `[project] dependencies` (updates use commit type `fix`) | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `project.optional-dependencies` | every array of `[project.optional-dependencies]` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `dependency-groups` | every array of `[dependency-groups]` (PEP 735) | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `tool.uv.dev-dependencies` | `[tool.uv] dev-dependencies` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `tool.pdm.dev-dependencies` | every array of `[tool.pdm.dev-dependencies]` (editable `-e …` entries are ignored) | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unconstrained` | no specifier, `*`, or only `!=` exclusions |
| `unsupported range` | a specifier that does not parse: a version that is not PEP 440 (`>=1.0-SNAPSHOT`, `===foobar`), a wildcard other than a trailing `.*` of `==` or `!=` (`~=1.*`, `>=1.*`), Poetry syntax (`^1.2`, `>=1 <2`, `\|\|`), or a bare version outside Pipfiles |
| `cannot locate value` | a TOML string with escapes |
| `url dependency` | `name @ https://…`, or a `[tool.uv.sources]` entry with `url` |
| `git dependency` | `name @ git+…`, or a `[tool.uv.sources]` entry with `git` |
| `local dependency` | `name @ file://…`, or a `[tool.uv.sources]` entry with `path` |
| `workspace member` | a `[tool.uv.sources]` entry with `workspace = true` |
| `multiple sources` | a `[tool.uv.sources]` entry that is an array (per-marker sources) |
| `unknown index <name>` | a `[tool.uv.sources]` `index` that no `[[tool.uv.index]]` names |
| `in-repository package (<file>)` | no index of the dep has the package (HTTP 404) but a scanned `pyproject.toml` defines it (`[project] name`, else `[tool.poetry] name`, PEP 503-normalized; `<file>` is the first such path), e.g. an unpublished package of the repository installed from a local build; a package an index has is updated as usual |

**Specifiers.**

- Every PEP 440 specifier set is accepted: `==`, `===`, `~=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` clauses separated by commas, with a trailing `.*` after `==` or `!=` (in a Pipfile also a bare version, meaning `==`). How a range is updated is described under Ranges.
- The dep's version is the range's anchor: in its last `||` alternative the first clause that is not `<`, `<=` or `!=` (`>=1.2,<2` → `1.2`, `<1.0.0,>=0.114.2` → `0.114.2`), else its first upper bound (`<2` → `2`). The anchor's precision is kept: candidates with non-zero parts beyond it are skipped (`precision`), others are cut to it (`>=1.2,<2` sees 3.1.0 as `3.1`). With a lockfile, the locked version takes the anchor's place.
- Versioning is `pep440`: pre and dev releases are only considered from a pre or dev release.
- Names are kept as written; the datasource looks them up PEP 503-normalized.

**Ranges (`rangeStrategy`).**

- `auto` (the default) is `update-lockfile`: a new version the range admits only moves the lockfile from the locked version (see Locked versions), and is not proposed without a lockfile deps reads; a version outside the range rewrites the range. Renovate's `auto` is `update-lockfile` for poetry and `replace` for pep621, pipenv and pip_requirements, which only differs where deps reads a lockfile.
- `bump` rewrites the range for every newer version, raising its lower bound (`>=1.2,<2` with 1.5.0 → `>=1.5.0,<2`, `^2.31` with 2.32.3 → `^2.32`, `>=2.31.0` → `>=2.32.3`). An admitted version a range has no bound to raise for (`<2`, `<=2`, `>1`, `==1.*`) is handled as under `update-lockfile`. `in-range-only` is `bump` without the versions outside the range.
- `replace` leaves admitted versions alone. `widen` does too, and for a version outside the range moves only its upper bounds (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=1.2,<4`); when that is not enough a Poetry constraint gets a new `||` alternative (`^2.13.0` → `^2.13.0 || ^3.0.0`) and any other range, like an exact version, is replaced. `pin` writes `==<version>` (an exact clause keeps its operator: `===1.4` → `===1.5.0`, Poetry `1.0` → `1.1`): a `pin` update to the locked version (else the newest version the range admits) unless another update shares its PR bucket, then every newer version.
- Rewrites follow Renovate's pep440 `getNewValue` (`lib/modules/versioning/pep440/range.ts`): an admitted version gets its `bump` rules, any other its `replace` rules (`widen` and `pin` aside, above), under every strategy (Renovate's `bump` would write the full new version as lower bound there too). Clause by clause: `!=` exclusions are kept verbatim; `<V` moves past the new version at the range's precision (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=3.1,<4`; with two clauses the precision is the first part in which the bounds differ, one finer for a major followed by `0`: `>=1.2.0,<2.0.0` with 3.1.4 → `>=3.1.4,<3.2.0`); `>=` and `>` take the new version at their own precision (`>=1.2` → `>=3.1`, a new version at or below them `>=<new>`); trailing zeros are trimmed when a clause has fewer than three parts; `~=`, `^` and `~` take the new version cut or zero-padded to their precision (`~=7.2` with 8.0.1 → `~=8.0`); `==`, `===`, `=`, a bare version and `<=` become the new version; wildcards keep `.*` at their precision (`==1.0.*` → `==1.2.*`).
- A Poetry constraint with `||` alternatives gets a new alternative for a version outside all of them (`^1 || ^2` with 3.0.0 → `^1 || ^2 || ^3`, as Renovate widens npm `||` ranges); `bump` raises the alternative that admits the version.
- Only the changed versions (and operators, `>` → `>=`) are rewritten; the bytes between clauses are kept. A rewrite that would not admit the new version (it is excluded by `!=`) is not proposed. Renovate's removal of a `>=` that a `==X.*` makes redundant is not done.

**Indexes.**

- A `[tool.uv.sources]` entry `{ index = "<name>" }` looks the dep up on that `[[tool.uv.index]]` URL only; otherwise the first index with `default = true` is used, else `PIP_INDEX_URL` or PyPI (see the `pypi` datasource), and the releases of every `[[tool.uv.index]]` that is neither `default` nor `explicit = true` are merged in.
- `[[tool.pdm.source]]` indexes are searched like pdm does: the source named `pypi` replaces PyPI, the other sources are extra indexes whose releases are merged in; a source whose `include_packages` match the (normalized) name is the only one searched for that dep, and one whose `exclude_packages` match is not searched for it. `type = "find_links"` sources are ignored, and so are URLs with `${VAR}` (a `pypi` one falls back to `PIP_INDEX_URL` or PyPI). A `[tool.uv.sources]` index takes precedence.
- Poetry 2 projects declare `[project] dependencies` too: they are extracted here, while `[tool.poetry.*]` tables belong to the `poetry` manager; both lock through `poetry.lock`.

**Locked versions.**

Before resolving, deps reads the lockfile the post-processor would update (see below) once per run: `[[package]]` `name` and `version` of `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock` and `pdm.lock`, and the `"==<version>"` pins of `Pipfile.lock` in the section of the dep's Pipfile table (`default` for `[packages]`, `develop` for `[dev-packages]`, else the category's name). Names compare PEP 503-normalized; a name locked at several versions (uv and pdm forks by marker) counts as not locked.

- The locked version is the current version (update types compare it with the new version), decides which versions the range admits are lockfile-only updates, and is what OSV is queried with, so an already locked fix is not proposed again. Without a lock, the range's anchor is used.
- A lockfile that does not parse is a run error (`<path>: <err>`); its deps count as not locked.

**Lockfile post-processing (`apply`, `run`).**

The lock directory of a `pyproject.toml` is its own directory when it holds `uv.lock` (uv), `poetry.lock` (Poetry) or `pdm.lock` (pdm). Its lockfile is regenerated in a temporary copy of that directory's top-level files (up to 4 MiB each; subdirectories are not copied) with the patched manifests and the current lockfile:

| Lockfile | Command | Without the tool in `PATH` |
|---|---|---|
| `uv.lock` | `uv lock --no-progress` | error `uv not found (needed to update uv.lock)` |
| `poetry.lock` | `poetry lock` (Poetry 2), `poetry lock --no-update` (Poetry 1), with `POETRY_NO_INTERACTION=1` | `uvx --from poetry poetry lock` |
| `pdm.lock` | `pdm lock --update-reuse` (keeps the pins the manifest still admits), with `PDM_CHECK_UPDATE=false PDM_NON_INTERACTIVE=1` | `uvx --from pdm pdm lock --update-reuse` |
| `Pipfile.lock` | `pipenv lock`, with `PIPENV_VENV_IN_PROJECT=1 PIPENV_IGNORE_VIRTUALENVS=1 PIPENV_NOSPIN=1 PIPENV_YES=1 PIPENV_VERBOSITY=-1` | `uvx --from pipenv pipenv lock` |

A `pyproject.toml` without a lockfile next to it belongs to the nearest `uv.lock` above whose `[tool.uv.workspace]` `members` (minus `exclude`) match its directory; every member's `pyproject.toml` is copied as well. Projects whose metadata is built (dynamic versions from VCS, local build backends) can fail to lock in the copy. A failure reports `<command> in <dir>: <last 20 output lines>`, and the directory's changes are dropped.

Lockfile-only updates (`rangeStrategy` `update-lockfile`, see Ranges) run after that regeneration, which is skipped when no manifest of the directory changed, with the same tool, environment and fallback:

| Lockfile | Lockfile-only command |
|---|---|
| `uv.lock` | `uv lock --no-progress --upgrade-package <name>==<version>…` |
| `poetry.lock` | `poetry update --lock <name>…` (Poetry 1 and 2) |
| `pdm.lock` | `pdm update --update-reuse --no-sync -G <group> <name>…`, once per lock group of the names (pdm takes one group with package names) |
| `Pipfile.lock` | `pipenv upgrade --lock-only --categories <category> <name>==<version>…`, once per Pipfile category |

Poetry and pdm cannot pin a version there: they move the dep to the newest version its range admits, which can be newer than proposed.

- `plan` does not run lock commands, and prints `note    uv.lock, poetry.lock, pdm.lock and Pipfile.lock changes are computed by apply/run`.

**Lock file maintenance (`run`).**

With [lockFileMaintenance](configuration.md#lockfilemaintenance) enabled, the lockfile of each lock directory of a scanned `pyproject.toml` (a uv workspace's root, as above) that post-processing updates is maintained when it is `uv.lock` or `pdm.lock` (`uv.lock` comes first); a `poetry.lock` is maintained by the `poetry` manager. Each is refreshed in the temporary copy described above, with the same environment and `uvx` fallback, which moves every locked package (transitive ones too) to the newest version the manifests admit; the manifests are not changed:

| Lockfile | Maintenance command |
|---|---|
| `uv.lock` | `uv lock --no-progress --upgrade` |
| `pdm.lock` | `pdm update --no-sync --update-all` (the locked groups are kept) |

All lockfiles share the PR on `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance`, which changes only lockfiles; `minimumReleaseAge` does not apply to it.

## pep723

Updates the PEP 508 requirement strings of PEP 723 inline script metadata: the TOML in the `# /// script` … `# ///` comment block of a Python script (as `uv run` and `pipx run` read it). The block's lines are parsed without their `# ` prefix at their own byte offsets, so only the specifier's versions inside the TOML string are rewritten. `requires-python` is no dep but drops the releases that do not support all of it (see the `pypi` datasource). A script has no lockfile deps reads.

**Files:**

- any `*.py` file with a `# /// script` block (Renovate's pep723 matches no file unless `managerFilePatterns` are set; deps reads every `.py` file and extracts nothing from files without block)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project.dependencies` | every string of the block's `dependencies` array (updates use commit type `fix`) | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unconstrained` | no specifier, `*`, or only `!=` exclusions |
| `unsupported range` | a specifier that does not parse: a version that is not PEP 440 (`>=1.0-SNAPSHOT`, `===foobar`), a wildcard other than a trailing `.*` of `==` or `!=` (`~=1.*`, `>=1.*`), Poetry syntax (`^1.2`, `>=1 <2`, `\|\|`), or a bare version outside Pipfiles |
| `cannot locate value` | a TOML string with escapes |
| `url dependency` | `name @ https://…` |
| `git dependency` | `name @ git+…` |
| `local dependency` | `name @ file://…` |

**Block.**

- The block starts at a line that is exactly `# /// script` and runs over the following comment lines (`#` alone or `# ` followed by text) up to the last line among them that is exactly `# ///` (PEP 723's reference regular expression); a block without that closing line is ignored. Only the first `script` block of a file is read.
- A block whose TOML does not parse is an extraction error of the file.

With a lockfile, the locked version takes the anchor's place.
- Versioning is `pep440`: pre and dev releases are only considered from a pre or dev release.
- Names are kept as written; the datasource looks them up PEP 503-normalized.

An admitted version a range has no bound to raise for (`<2`, `<=2`, `>1`, `==1.*`) is handled as under `update-lockfile`. `in-range-only` is `bump` without the versions outside the range.
- `replace` leaves admitted versions alone. `widen` does too, and for a version outside the range moves only its upper bounds (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=1.2,<4`); when that is not enough a Poetry constraint gets a new `||` alternative (`^2.13.0` → `^2.13.0 || ^3.0.0`) and any other range, like an exact version, is replaced. `pin` writes `==<version>` (an exact clause keeps its operator: `===1.4` → `===1.5.0`, Poetry `1.0` → `1.1`): a `pin` update to the locked version (else the newest version the range admits) unless another update shares its PR bucket, then every newer version.
- Rewrites follow Renovate's pep440 `getNewValue` (`lib/modules/versioning/pep440/range.ts`): an admitted version gets its `bump` rules, any other its `replace` rules (`widen` and `pin` aside, above), under every strategy (Renovate's `bump` would write the full new version as lower bound there too). Clause by clause: `!=` exclusions are kept verbatim; `<V` moves past the new version at the range's precision (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=3.1,<4`; with two clauses the precision is the first part in which the bounds differ, one finer for a major followed by `0`: `>=1.2.0,<2.0.0` with 3.1.4 → `>=3.1.4,<3.2.0`); `>=` and `>` take the new version at their own precision (`>=1.2` → `>=3.1`, a new version at or below them `>=<new>`); trailing zeros are trimmed when a clause has fewer than three parts; `~=`, `^` and `~` take the new version cut or zero-padded to their precision (`~=7.2` with 8.0.1 → `~=8.0`); `==`, `===`, `=`, a bare version and `<=` become the new version; wildcards keep `.*` at their precision (`==1.0.*` → `==1.2.*`).
- A Poetry constraint with `||` alternatives gets a new alternative for a version outside all of them (`^1 || ^2` with 3.0.0 → `^1 || ^2 || ^3`, as Renovate widens npm `||` ranges); `bump` raises the alternative that admits the version.
- Only the changed versions (and operators, `>` → `>=`) are rewritten; the bytes between clauses are kept. A rewrite that would not admit the new version (it is excluded by `!=`) is not proposed. Renovate's removal of a `>=` that a `==X.*` makes redundant is not done.

## setup-cfg

Updates the PEP 508 requirements of setuptools' declarative configuration in `setup.cfg`. A requirement value is the rest of its key line plus the indented continuation lines, one requirement per line (`;`-separated on the key line, as setuptools' `list-semi`); only the specifier's versions are rewritten. `#`/`;` comment lines and inline `#` comments are ignored, and so are `file:` and `attr:` directives (a `file: requirements.txt` is read by the `pip_requirements` manager when its name matches). `[options] python_requires` is no dep but drops the releases that do not support all of it (see the `pypi` datasource). A `setup.cfg` has no lockfile.

**Files:**

- any `setup.cfg`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `install` | `[options] install_requires` (updates use commit type `fix`) | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `setup` | `[options] setup_requires` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `test` | `[options] tests_require` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `extra` | every key of `[options.extras_require]` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unconstrained` | no specifier, `*`, or only `!=` exclusions |
| `unsupported range` | a specifier that does not parse: a version that is not PEP 440 (`>=1.0-SNAPSHOT`, `===foobar`), a wildcard other than a trailing `.*` of `==` or `!=` (`~=1.*`, `>=1.*`), Poetry syntax (`^1.2`, `>=1 <2`, `\|\|`), or a bare version outside Pipfiles |
| `url dependency` | `name @ https://…` |
| `git dependency` | `name @ git+…` |
| `local dependency` | `name @ file://…` |

**Specifiers.**

- Every PEP 440 specifier set is accepted: `==`, `===`, `~=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` clauses separated by commas, with a trailing `.*` after `==` or `!=` (in a Pipfile also a bare version, meaning `==`). How a range is updated is described under Ranges.
- The dep's version is the range's anchor: in its last `||` alternative the first clause that is not `<`, `<=` or `!=` (`>=1.2,<2` → `1.2`, `<1.0.0,>=0.114.2` → `0.114.2`), else its first upper bound (`<2` → `2`). The anchor's precision is kept: candidates with non-zero parts beyond it are skipped (`precision`), others are cut to it (`>=1.2,<2` sees 3.1.0 as `3.1`). With a lockfile, the locked version takes the anchor's place.
- Versioning is `pep440`: pre and dev releases are only considered from a pre or dev release.
- Names are kept as written; the datasource looks them up PEP 503-normalized.

**Ranges (`rangeStrategy`).**

- `auto` (the default) is `update-lockfile`: a new version the range admits only moves the lockfile from the locked version (see Locked versions), and is not proposed without a lockfile deps reads; a version outside the range rewrites the range. Renovate's `auto` is `update-lockfile` for poetry and `replace` for pep621, pipenv and pip_requirements, which only differs where deps reads a lockfile.
- `bump` rewrites the range for every newer version, raising its lower bound (`>=1.2,<2` with 1.5.0 → `>=1.5.0,<2`, `^2.31` with 2.32.3 → `^2.32`, `>=2.31.0` → `>=2.32.3`). An admitted version a range has no bound to raise for (`<2`, `<=2`, `>1`, `==1.*`) is handled as under `update-lockfile`. `in-range-only` is `bump` without the versions outside the range.
- `replace` leaves admitted versions alone. `widen` does too, and for a version outside the range moves only its upper bounds (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=1.2,<4`); when that is not enough a Poetry constraint gets a new `||` alternative (`^2.13.0` → `^2.13.0 || ^3.0.0`) and any other range, like an exact version, is replaced. `pin` writes `==<version>` (an exact clause keeps its operator: `===1.4` → `===1.5.0`, Poetry `1.0` → `1.1`): a `pin` update to the locked version (else the newest version the range admits) unless another update shares its PR bucket, then every newer version.
- Rewrites follow Renovate's pep440 `getNewValue` (`lib/modules/versioning/pep440/range.ts`): an admitted version gets its `bump` rules, any other its `replace` rules (`widen` and `pin` aside, above), under every strategy (Renovate's `bump` would write the full new version as lower bound there too). Clause by clause: `!=` exclusions are kept verbatim; `<V` moves past the new version at the range's precision (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=3.1,<4`; with two clauses the precision is the first part in which the bounds differ, one finer for a major followed by `0`: `>=1.2.0,<2.0.0` with 3.1.4 → `>=3.1.4,<3.2.0`); `>=` and `>` take the new version at their own precision (`>=1.2` → `>=3.1`, a new version at or below them `>=<new>`); trailing zeros are trimmed when a clause has fewer than three parts; `~=`, `^` and `~` take the new version cut or zero-padded to their precision (`~=7.2` with 8.0.1 → `~=8.0`); `==`, `===`, `=`, a bare version and `<=` become the new version; wildcards keep `.*` at their precision (`==1.0.*` → `==1.2.*`).
- A Poetry constraint with `||` alternatives gets a new alternative for a version outside all of them (`^1 || ^2` with 3.0.0 → `^1 || ^2 || ^3`, as Renovate widens npm `||` ranges); `bump` raises the alternative that admits the version.
- Only the changed versions (and operators, `>` → `>=`) are rewritten; the bytes between clauses are kept. A rewrite that would not admit the new version (it is excluded by `!=`) is not proposed. Renovate's removal of a `>=` that a `==X.*` makes redundant is not done.

## pip_setup

Updates the requirement string literals of `setup.py` files. As Renovate's pip_setup, the file is lexed as Python but not evaluated: every plain string literal (`'…'` or `"…"`, also `r`/`u`-prefixed) that is a PEP 508 requirement with a version specifier (`"requests>=2.31"`, `'django[argon2]~=5.0; python_version>="3.10"'`) is a dep, wherever it is written (in `setup()`, a list variable, a dict of extras). Literals without specifier or whose specifier does not parse as PEP 440 (entry points such as `'cli=pkg.main:run'`), with escapes, triple-quoted, f-strings and bytes are not, nor are operands of `+`, `*` or `%` and receivers of a method call (`"x>={}".format(v)`), so requirements built at runtime or read from files yield no deps. Only the specifier's versions inside the literal are rewritten. A `setup.py` has no lockfile.

**Files:**

- any `setup.py`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `install` | a literal in the `install_requires=` keyword argument | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `setup` | a literal in `setup_requires=` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `test` | a literal in `tests_require=` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `extra` | a literal in `extras_require=` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `other` | any other requirement literal (a module-level `REQUIRES = [...]` passed by name; Renovate sets no dep type) | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unconstrained` | no specifier, `*`, or only `!=` exclusions |
| `ignored` | the literal is followed on its line (after an optional `,`) by a `# renovate: ignore` comment |

**Specifiers.**

- Every PEP 440 specifier set is accepted: `==`, `===`, `~=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` clauses separated by commas, with a trailing `.*` after `==` or `!=` (in a Pipfile also a bare version, meaning `==`). How a range is updated is described under Ranges.

The anchor's precision is kept: candidates with non-zero parts beyond it are skipped (`precision`), others are cut to it (`>=1.2,<2` sees 3.1.0 as `3.1`). With a lockfile, the locked version takes the anchor's place.
- Versioning is `pep440`: pre and dev releases are only considered from a pre or dev release.
- Names are kept as written; the datasource looks them up PEP 503-normalized.

**Ranges (`rangeStrategy`).**

An admitted version a range has no bound to raise for (`<2`, `<=2`, `>1`, `==1.*`) is handled as under `update-lockfile`. `in-range-only` is `bump` without the versions outside the range.
- `replace` leaves admitted versions alone. `widen` does too, and for a version outside the range moves only its upper bounds (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=1.2,<4`); when that is not enough a Poetry constraint gets a new `||` alternative (`^2.13.0` → `^2.13.0 || ^3.0.0`) and any other range, like an exact version, is replaced. `pin` writes `==<version>` (an exact clause keeps its operator: `===1.4` → `===1.5.0`, Poetry `1.0` → `1.1`): a `pin` update to the locked version (else the newest version the range admits) unless another update shares its PR bucket, then every newer version.

## poetry

Updates the Poetry dependency tables of `pyproject.toml`, then refreshes `poetry.lock`. The file is parsed with byte spans; only the constraint's versions inside the TOML string are rewritten. The `python` entry (else `[project] requires-python`) is no dep but drops the releases that do not support all of it (see the `pypi` datasource); `[project]` dependencies of Poetry 2 projects belong to the `pep621` manager.

**Files:**

- `pyproject.toml`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dependencies` | `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` (updates use commit type `fix`) | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `dev-dependencies` | `[tool.poetry.dev-dependencies]` (Poetry 1.0/1.1) | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `group` | `[tool.poetry.group.<name>.dependencies]` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unconstrained` | `*`, empty, only `!=` exclusions, or a table without `version` |
| `unsupported range` | a constraint that does not parse: a version that is not PEP 440, a wildcard other than a trailing `.*` of `==`, `!=` or a bare version (`^1.*`), non-string values |
| `cannot locate value` | a TOML string with escapes |
| `git dependency` | `{ git = … }` |
| `local dependency` | `{ path = … }` |
| `url dependency` | `{ url = … }` |
| `multiple constraints` | an array of constraint tables (per-marker constraints) |
| `unknown source <name>` | a `source` that no `[[tool.poetry.source]]` names |
| `in-repository package (<file>)` | no index of the dep has the package (HTTP 404) but a scanned `pyproject.toml` defines it (`[project] name`, else `[tool.poetry] name`, PEP 503-normalized; `<file>` is the first such path), e.g. an unpublished package of the repository installed from a local build; a package an index has is updated as usual |

**Constraints.**

- Every Poetry constraint is accepted: the PEP 440 clauses plus `^`, `~`, `=` and a bare version (an exact pin; `2.*` a wildcard), separated by commas or spaces (`>=1.2 <2`), with `||` (or `|`) alternatives (`^1 || ^2`). How a constraint is updated is described under Ranges.
- The dep's version is the range's anchor: in its last `||` alternative the first clause that is not `<`, `<=` or `!=` (`>=1.2,<2` → `1.2`, `<1.0.0,>=0.114.2` → `0.114.2`), else its first upper bound (`<2` → `2`). The anchor's precision is kept: candidates with non-zero parts beyond it are skipped (`precision`), others are cut to it (`>=1.2,<2` sees 3.1.0 as `3.1`). With a lockfile, the locked version takes the anchor's place.
- Versioning is `pep440`: pre and dev releases are only considered from a pre or dev release.

**Ranges (`rangeStrategy`).**

- `auto` (the default) is `update-lockfile`: a new version the range admits only moves the lockfile from the locked version (see Locked versions), and is not proposed without a lockfile deps reads; a version outside the range rewrites the range. Renovate's `auto` is `update-lockfile` for poetry and `replace` for pep621, pipenv and pip_requirements, which only differs where deps reads a lockfile.
- `bump` rewrites the range for every newer version, raising its lower bound (`>=1.2,<2` with 1.5.0 → `>=1.5.0,<2`, `^2.31` with 2.32.3 → `^2.32`, `>=2.31.0` → `>=2.32.3`). An admitted version a range has no bound to raise for (`<2`, `<=2`, `>1`, `==1.*`) is handled as under `update-lockfile`. `in-range-only` is `bump` without the versions outside the range.
- `replace` leaves admitted versions alone. `widen` does too, and for a version outside the range moves only its upper bounds (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=1.2,<4`); when that is not enough a Poetry constraint gets a new `||` alternative (`^2.13.0` → `^2.13.0 || ^3.0.0`) and any other range, like an exact version, is replaced. `pin` writes `==<version>` (an exact clause keeps its operator: `===1.4` → `===1.5.0`, Poetry `1.0` → `1.1`): a `pin` update to the locked version (else the newest version the range admits) unless another update shares its PR bucket, then every newer version.
- Rewrites follow Renovate's pep440 `getNewValue` (`lib/modules/versioning/pep440/range.ts`): an admitted version gets its `bump` rules, any other its `replace` rules (`widen` and `pin` aside, above), under every strategy (Renovate's `bump` would write the full new version as lower bound there too). Clause by clause: `!=` exclusions are kept verbatim; `<V` moves past the new version at the range's precision (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=3.1,<4`; with two clauses the precision is the first part in which the bounds differ, one finer for a major followed by `0`: `>=1.2.0,<2.0.0` with 3.1.4 → `>=3.1.4,<3.2.0`); `>=` and `>` take the new version at their own precision (`>=1.2` → `>=3.1`, a new version at or below them `>=<new>`); trailing zeros are trimmed when a clause has fewer than three parts; `~=`, `^` and `~` take the new version cut or zero-padded to their precision (`~=7.2` with 8.0.1 → `~=8.0`); `==`, `===`, `=`, a bare version and `<=` become the new version; wildcards keep `.*` at their precision (`==1.0.*` → `==1.2.*`).
- A Poetry constraint with `||` alternatives gets a new alternative for a version outside all of them (`^1 || ^2` with 3.0.0 → `^1 || ^2 || ^3`, as Renovate widens npm `||` ranges); `bump` raises the alternative that admits the version.
- Only the changed versions (and operators, `>` → `>=`) are rewritten; the bytes between clauses are kept. A rewrite that would not admit the new version (it is excluded by `!=`) is not proposed. Renovate's removal of a `>=` that a `==X.*` makes redundant is not done.

**Sources.**

- Values are a constraint string or a table with `version` (`{ version = "^2.0", extras = ["socks"] }`).
- A table's `source = "<name>"` looks the dep up on that `[[tool.poetry.source]]` URL only; otherwise the first source with `priority = "primary"` or `"default"` (or the legacy `default = true`) is used, else `PIP_INDEX_URL` or PyPI (see the `pypi` datasource), and the releases of every `priority = "supplemental"` source are merged in. `explicit` sources serve only deps that name them.

**Locked versions.**

Before resolving, deps reads the lockfile the post-processor would update (see below) once per run: `[[package]]` `name` and `version` of `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock` and `pdm.lock`, and the `"==<version>"` pins of `Pipfile.lock` in the section of the dep's Pipfile table (`default` for `[packages]`, `develop` for `[dev-packages]`, else the category's name). Names compare PEP 503-normalized; a name locked at several versions (uv and pdm forks by marker) counts as not locked.

- The locked version is the current version (update types compare it with the new version), decides which versions the range admits are lockfile-only updates, and is what OSV is queried with, so an already locked fix is not proposed again. Without a lock, the range's anchor is used.
- A lockfile that does not parse is a run error (`<path>: <err>`); its deps count as not locked.

**Lockfile post-processing (`apply`, `run`).**

The lock directory of a `pyproject.toml` is its own directory when it holds `poetry.lock`. Its lockfile is regenerated in a temporary copy of that directory's top-level files (up to 4 MiB each; subdirectories are not copied) with the patched manifests and the current lockfile:

| Lockfile | Command | Without the tool in `PATH` |
|---|---|---|
| `uv.lock` | `uv lock --no-progress` | error `uv not found (needed to update uv.lock)` |
| `poetry.lock` | `poetry lock` (Poetry 2), `poetry lock --no-update` (Poetry 1), with `POETRY_NO_INTERACTION=1` | `uvx --from poetry poetry lock` |
| `pdm.lock` | `pdm lock --update-reuse` (keeps the pins the manifest still admits), with `PDM_CHECK_UPDATE=false PDM_NON_INTERACTIVE=1` | `uvx --from pdm pdm lock --update-reuse` |
| `Pipfile.lock` | `pipenv lock`, with `PIPENV_VENV_IN_PROJECT=1 PIPENV_IGNORE_VIRTUALENVS=1 PIPENV_NOSPIN=1 PIPENV_YES=1 PIPENV_VERBOSITY=-1` | `uvx --from pipenv pipenv lock` |

A `pyproject.toml` without a lockfile next to it belongs to the nearest `uv.lock` above whose `[tool.uv.workspace]` `members` (minus `exclude`) match its directory; every member's `pyproject.toml` is copied as well. Projects whose metadata is built (dynamic versions from VCS, local build backends) can fail to lock in the copy. A failure reports `<command> in <dir>: <last 20 output lines>`, and the directory's changes are dropped.

Lockfile-only updates (`rangeStrategy` `update-lockfile`, see Ranges) run after that regeneration, which is skipped when no manifest of the directory changed, with the same tool, environment and fallback:

| Lockfile | Lockfile-only command |
|---|---|
| `uv.lock` | `uv lock --no-progress --upgrade-package <name>==<version>…` |
| `poetry.lock` | `poetry update --lock <name>…` (Poetry 1 and 2) |
| `pdm.lock` | `pdm update --update-reuse --no-sync -G <group> <name>…`, once per lock group of the names (pdm takes one group with package names) |
| `Pipfile.lock` | `pipenv upgrade --lock-only --categories <category> <name>==<version>…`, once per Pipfile category |

Poetry and pdm cannot pin a version there: they move the dep to the newest version its range admits, which can be newer than proposed.

- `plan` does not run lock commands, and prints `note    uv.lock, poetry.lock, pdm.lock and Pipfile.lock changes are computed by apply/run`.

**Lock file maintenance (`run`).**

With [lockFileMaintenance](configuration.md#lockfilemaintenance) enabled, the `poetry.lock` of each lock directory of a scanned `pyproject.toml` is maintained, also of Poetry 2 projects with only `[project]` dependencies; a directory that also holds `uv.lock` is the `pep621` manager's, whose `uv.lock` is maintained instead. Each is refreshed in the temporary copy described above, with the same environment and `uvx` fallback, which moves every locked package (transitive ones too) to the newest version the manifests admit; the manifests are not changed:

| Lockfile | Maintenance command |
|---|---|
| `poetry.lock` | `poetry update --lock` (Poetry 1 and 2) |

All lockfiles share the PR on `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance`, which changes only lockfiles; `minimumReleaseAge` does not apply to it.

## pipenv

Updates the packages of a `Pipfile`, then refreshes `Pipfile.lock`. The file is parsed with byte spans; only the specifier's versions inside the TOML string are rewritten. `[requires]` is no dep: `python_full_version` (exactly) else `python_version` (`3.11` → `==3.11.*`) drops the releases that do not support it (see the `pypi` datasource).

**Files:**

- `Pipfile`

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `packages` | `[packages]` (updates use commit type `fix`) | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |
| `dev-packages` | `[dev-packages]` | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |

| `git dependency` | `{ git = … }` |
| `local dependency` | `{ path = … }` |
| `url dependency` | `{ file = … }` |
| `unknown index <name>` | an `index` that no `[[source]]` names |

With a lockfile, the locked version takes the anchor's place.

- Names are kept as written; the datasource looks them up PEP 503-normalized.

- `auto` (the default) is `update-lockfile`: a new version the range admits only moves the lockfile from the locked version (see Locked versions), and is not proposed without a lockfile deps reads; a version outside the range rewrites the range. Renovate's `auto` is `update-lockfile` for poetry and `replace` for pep621, pipenv and pip_requirements, which only differs where deps reads a lockfile.
- `bump` rewrites the range for every newer version, raising its lower bound (`>=1.2,<2` with 1.5.0 → `>=1.5.0,<2`, `^2.31` with 2.32.3 → `^2.32`, `>=2.31.0` → `>=2.32.3`). An admitted version a range has no bound to raise for (`<2`, `<=2`, `>1`, `==1.*`) is handled as under `update-lockfile`. `in-range-only` is `bump` without the versions outside the range.
- `replace` leaves admitted versions alone. `widen` does too, and for a version outside the range moves only its upper bounds (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=1.2,<4`); when that is not enough a Poetry constraint gets a new `||` alternative (`^2.13.0` → `^2.13.0 || ^3.0.0`) and any other range, like an exact version, is replaced. `pin` writes `==<version>` (an exact clause keeps its operator: `===1.4` → `===1.5.0`, Poetry `1.0` → `1.1`): a `pin` update to the locked version (else the newest version the range admits) unless another update shares its PR bucket, then every newer version.
- Rewrites follow Renovate's pep440 `getNewValue` (`lib/modules/versioning/pep440/range.ts`): an admitted version gets its `bump` rules, any other its `replace` rules (`widen` and `pin` aside, above), under every strategy (Renovate's `bump` would write the full new version as lower bound there too). Clause by clause: `!=` exclusions are kept verbatim; `<V` moves past the new version at the range's precision (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=3.1,<4`; with two clauses the precision is the first part in which the bounds differ, one finer for a major followed by `0`: `>=1.2.0,<2.0.0` with 3.1.4 → `>=3.1.4,<3.2.0`); `>=` and `>` take the new version at their own precision (`>=1.2` → `>=3.1`, a new version at or below them `>=<new>`); trailing zeros are trimmed when a clause has fewer than three parts; `~=`, `^` and `~` take the new version cut or zero-padded to their precision (`~=7.2` with 8.0.1 → `~=8.0`); `==`, `===`, `=`, a bare version and `<=` become the new version; wildcards keep `.*` at their precision (`==1.0.*` → `==1.2.*`).
- A Poetry constraint with `||` alternatives gets a new alternative for a version outside all of them (`^1 || ^2` with 3.0.0 → `^1 || ^2 || ^3`, as Renovate widens npm `||` ranges); `bump` raises the alternative that admits the version.
- Only the changed versions (and operators, `>` → `>=`) are rewritten; the bytes between clauses are kept. A rewrite that would not admit the new version (it is excluded by `!=`) is not proposed. Renovate's removal of a `>=` that a `==X.*` makes redundant is not done.

**Indexes.**

- Values are a specifier string or a table with `version` (`{ version = "==2.0", extras = ["socks"] }`).
- A table's `index = "<name>"` looks the dep up on that `[[source]]` URL; any other dep uses the first `[[source]]`, and with `[pipenv] install_search_all_sources = true` also merges in the releases of the other sources (pipenv ≥ 2022.3 otherwise resolves it on the first only). A source URL with `${VAR}` is not expanded and falls back to `PIP_INDEX_URL` or PyPI (see the `pypi` datasource).

**Locked versions.**

Before resolving, deps reads the lockfile the post-processor would update (see below) once per run: `[[package]]` `name` and `version` of `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock` and `pdm.lock`, and the `"==<version>"` pins of `Pipfile.lock` in the section of the dep's Pipfile table (`default` for `[packages]`, `develop` for `[dev-packages]`, else the category's name). Names compare PEP 503-normalized; a name locked at several versions (uv and pdm forks by marker) counts as not locked.

- The locked version is the current version (update types compare it with the new version), decides which versions the range admits are lockfile-only updates, and is what OSV is queried with, so an already locked fix is not proposed again. Without a lock, the range's anchor is used.
- A lockfile that does not parse is a run error (`<path>: <err>`); its deps count as not locked.

**Lockfile post-processing (`apply`, `run`).**

The lock directory of a `Pipfile` is its own directory when it holds `Pipfile.lock`. Its lockfile is regenerated in a temporary copy of that directory's top-level files (up to 4 MiB each; subdirectories are not copied) with the patched manifests and the current lockfile:

| Lockfile | Command | Without the tool in `PATH` |
|---|---|---|
| `uv.lock` | `uv lock --no-progress` | error `uv not found (needed to update uv.lock)` |
| `poetry.lock` | `poetry lock` (Poetry 2), `poetry lock --no-update` (Poetry 1), with `POETRY_NO_INTERACTION=1` | `uvx --from poetry poetry lock` |
| `pdm.lock` | `pdm lock --update-reuse` (keeps the pins the manifest still admits), with `PDM_CHECK_UPDATE=false PDM_NON_INTERACTIVE=1` | `uvx --from pdm pdm lock --update-reuse` |
| `Pipfile.lock` | `pipenv lock`, with `PIPENV_VENV_IN_PROJECT=1 PIPENV_IGNORE_VIRTUALENVS=1 PIPENV_NOSPIN=1 PIPENV_YES=1 PIPENV_VERBOSITY=-1` | `uvx --from pipenv pipenv lock` |

A `pyproject.toml` without a lockfile next to it belongs to the nearest `uv.lock` above whose `[tool.uv.workspace]` `members` (minus `exclude`) match its directory; every member's `pyproject.toml` is copied as well. Projects whose metadata is built (dynamic versions from VCS, local build backends) can fail to lock in the copy. A failure reports `<command> in <dir>: <last 20 output lines>`, and the directory's changes are dropped.

Lockfile-only updates (`rangeStrategy` `update-lockfile`, see Ranges) run after that regeneration, which is skipped when no manifest of the directory changed, with the same tool, environment and fallback:

| Lockfile | Lockfile-only command |
|---|---|
| `uv.lock` | `uv lock --no-progress --upgrade-package <name>==<version>…` |
| `poetry.lock` | `poetry update --lock <name>…` (Poetry 1 and 2) |
| `pdm.lock` | `pdm update --update-reuse --no-sync -G <group> <name>…`, once per lock group of the names (pdm takes one group with package names) |
| `Pipfile.lock` | `pipenv upgrade --lock-only --categories <category> <name>==<version>…`, once per Pipfile category |

Poetry and pdm cannot pin a version there: they move the dep to the newest version its range admits, which can be newer than proposed.

- `plan` does not run lock commands, and prints `note    uv.lock, poetry.lock, pdm.lock and Pipfile.lock changes are computed by apply/run`.

**Lock file maintenance (`run`).**

With [lockFileMaintenance](configuration.md#lockfilemaintenance) enabled, the `Pipfile.lock` next to each scanned `Pipfile` is maintained, unless the directory also holds a `pyproject.toml` with `uv.lock`, `poetry.lock` or `pdm.lock`: only that lockfile is maintained there (by the `pep621` or `poetry` manager). Each is refreshed in the temporary copy described above, with the same environment and `uvx` fallback, which moves every locked package (transitive ones too) to the newest version the manifests admit; the manifests are not changed:

| Lockfile | Maintenance command |
|---|---|
| `Pipfile.lock` | `pipenv lock` (pipenv resolves every package anew) |

All lockfiles share the PR on `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance`, which changes only lockfiles; `minimumReleaseAge` does not apply to it.

## homeassistant-manifest

Updates the PEP 508 `requirements` of Home Assistant integration manifests (`custom_components/<domain>/manifest.json`, or the integrations of Home Assistant core). Only the specifier's versions inside the JSON string are rewritten; the file keeps its formatting. There is no lockfile.

**Files:**

- `manifest.json` at any depth whose top-level object has string `domain` and `name` members (other `manifest.json` files, such as web app or browser extension manifests, have no deps)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `requirements` | every string of `requirements` (`"alexapy==1.34.0"`, `"dictor>=0.1.12,<0.2"`); non-string items are ignored | `pypi` | `pep440` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unconstrained` | no specifier, `*`, or only `!=` exclusions |
| `unsupported range` | a specifier that does not parse: a version that is not PEP 440 (`>=1.0-SNAPSHOT`, `===foobar`), a wildcard other than a trailing `.*` of `==` or `!=` (`~=1.*`, `>=1.*`), Poetry syntax (`^1.2`, `>=1 <2`, `\|\|`), or a bare version outside Pipfiles |
| `cannot locate value` | a JSON string with escapes |
| `url dependency` | `name @ https://…` |
| `git dependency` | `name @ git+…` |
| `local dependency` | `name @ file://…` |
| `invalid dependency specification` | a requirement that does not start with a valid project name |

**Specifiers.**

- Every PEP 440 specifier set is accepted: `==`, `===`, `~=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` clauses separated by commas, with a trailing `.*` after `==` or `!=` (in a Pipfile also a bare version, meaning `==`). How a range is updated is described under Ranges.
- The dep's version is the range's anchor: in its last `||` alternative the first clause that is not `<`, `<=` or `!=` (`>=1.2,<2` → `1.2`, `<1.0.0,>=0.114.2` → `0.114.2`), else its first upper bound (`<2` → `2`). The anchor's precision is kept: candidates with non-zero parts beyond it are skipped (`precision`), others are cut to it (`>=1.2,<2` sees 3.1.0 as `3.1`). With a lockfile, the locked version takes the anchor's place.
- Versioning is `pep440`: pre and dev releases are only considered from a pre or dev release.
- Names are kept as written; the datasource looks them up PEP 503-normalized.

**Ranges (`rangeStrategy`).**

- `auto` (the default) is `update-lockfile`: a new version the range admits only moves the lockfile from the locked version (see Locked versions), and is not proposed without a lockfile deps reads; a version outside the range rewrites the range. Renovate's `auto` is `update-lockfile` for poetry and `replace` for pep621, pipenv and pip_requirements, which only differs where deps reads a lockfile.
- `bump` rewrites the range for every newer version, raising its lower bound (`>=1.2,<2` with 1.5.0 → `>=1.5.0,<2`, `^2.31` with 2.32.3 → `^2.32`, `>=2.31.0` → `>=2.32.3`). An admitted version a range has no bound to raise for (`<2`, `<=2`, `>1`, `==1.*`) is handled as under `update-lockfile`. `in-range-only` is `bump` without the versions outside the range.
- `replace` leaves admitted versions alone. `widen` does too, and for a version outside the range moves only its upper bounds (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=1.2,<4`); when that is not enough a Poetry constraint gets a new `||` alternative (`^2.13.0` → `^2.13.0 || ^3.0.0`) and any other range, like an exact version, is replaced. `pin` writes `==<version>` (an exact clause keeps its operator: `===1.4` → `===1.5.0`, Poetry `1.0` → `1.1`): a `pin` update to the locked version (else the newest version the range admits) unless another update shares its PR bucket, then every newer version.
- Rewrites follow Renovate's pep440 `getNewValue` (`lib/modules/versioning/pep440/range.ts`): an admitted version gets its `bump` rules, any other its `replace` rules (`widen` and `pin` aside, above), under every strategy (Renovate's `bump` would write the full new version as lower bound there too). Clause by clause: `!=` exclusions are kept verbatim; `<V` moves past the new version at the range's precision (`>=1.2,<2` with 3.1.0 → `>=3.1,<4`; with two clauses the precision is the first part in which the bounds differ, one finer for a major followed by `0`: `>=1.2.0,<2.0.0` with 3.1.4 → `>=3.1.4,<3.2.0`); `>=` and `>` take the new version at their own precision (`>=1.2` → `>=3.1`, a new version at or below them `>=<new>`); trailing zeros are trimmed when a clause has fewer than three parts; `~=`, `^` and `~` take the new version cut or zero-padded to their precision (`~=7.2` with 8.0.1 → `~=8.0`); `==`, `===`, `=`, a bare version and `<=` become the new version; wildcards keep `.*` at their precision (`==1.0.*` → `==1.2.*`).
- A Poetry constraint with `||` alternatives gets a new alternative for a version outside all of them (`^1 || ^2` with 3.0.0 → `^1 || ^2 || ^3`, as Renovate widens npm `||` ranges); `bump` raises the alternative that admits the version.
- Only the changed versions (and operators, `>` → `>=`) are rewritten; the bytes between clauses are kept. A rewrite that would not admit the new version (it is excluded by `!=`) is not proposed. Renovate's removal of a `>=` that a `==X.*` makes redundant is not done.

## conda

Updates the packages of conda environment files: the match specs of `dependencies`, looked up on the file's anaconda.org `channels`, and the requirements of the nested `pip:` list, looked up on PyPI (Dependabot's `conda` ecosystem; Renovate has no conda manager). The file is parsed as YAML with byte spans; only the version spec of an entry is rewritten. There is no lockfile (`conda-lock.yml` is not maintained).

**Files:**

- `environment.yml`, `environment.yaml` (any directory)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dependencies` | `dependencies` match specs: `numpy=1.26` (fuzzy: any 1.26.x), `numpy==1.26.4`, `numpy>=1.26,<2`, `numpy 1.26.*`, `numpy >=1.26`, with a channel prefix `conda-forge::numpy=1.26` | `conda` | `conda` | updated |
| `pip` | the PEP 508 requirements of a `- pip:` list in `dependencies` (`requests>=2.31`, `black==24.4.2`) | `pypi` (the list's `--index-url`, `--extra-index-url`) | `pep440` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unconstrained` | a package without version spec (`numpy`, `numpy *`) or with only exclusions (`numpy!=1.26.0`) |
| `build string` | a match spec with a build string (`numpy=1.26.4=py312h8753938_0`, `numpy 1.26.4 py312_0`): it pins a build of one version (as Dependabot, deps does not update it) |
| `unsupported match spec` | the bracket form (`numpy[version='>=1.26']`) or `\|` alternatives (`numpy=1.25\|1.26`) |
| `unsupported range` | a version spec conda's VersionSpec does not read (`numpy>=1.26.*`, `numpy=latest`), or a pip requirement that is no PEP 508 requirement |
| `unsupported channel <channel>` | a `<channel>::` prefix, or a `channels` list without any entry, that the anaconda.org API does not serve: a URL of another host (`https://prefix.dev/conda-forge`), a local or `file://` channel |
| `cannot locate value` | a value whose YAML bytes differ from its text (escapes, block scalars) |
| `git dependency` | a pip requirement that is a VCS URL (`git+https://…`), also as `name @ git+https://…` |
| `local dependency` | a pip requirement that is a path (`./pkg`, `file:…`) |
| `url dependency` | a pip requirement that is another URL (`https://…/pkg.whl`, `name @ https://…`) |

**Channels.**

- A package is looked up on the `channels` of the file in order; the first channel that has it answers, as with conda's strict channel priority. Without `channels`, on `conda-forge` (Dependabot's and Renovate's default).
- A `<channel>::` prefix (`pytorch::pytorch`, `conda-forge/linux-64::numpy`) looks the package up on that channel only.
- Channel names keep their name (`/label/<x>` and `/<subdir>` suffixes dropped); `defaults` is the anaconda.org `anaconda` channel (a mirror of Anaconda's main repository), and so is `https://repo.anaconda.com/pkgs/main`; `https://conda.anaconda.org/<channel>` URLs name `<channel>`. `nodefaults`, URLs of other hosts and local channels are not looked up.

**Versions (`conda` versioning).**

- Versions are compared with conda's VersionOrder: `[<epoch>!]<version>[+<local>]`, segments separated by `.` or `_`, each a run of numbers and words; a word sorts below a number (`1.1.1w` < `1.1.1`, `1.0rc1` < `1.0`), `dev` below every other word, `post` above every number. Dependabot and Renovate both use conda's ordering for conda packages (Renovate's `conda` versioning, Dependabot's Conda::Version), not PEP 440, which rejects versions such as `1.1.1w`, `2024a` or `9e`.
- A version with a `dev`, `rc`, `alpha`, `beta`, `pre` or `preview` word, or an `a`, `b` or `c` followed by a number (`2.0b1`), is a prerelease, proposed only from a prerelease. Other words are part of the release (`1.1.1w`, `2024a`, `9e`).
- The first segment decides major updates, the second minor ones, anything after patch ones.
- As for pep440, a candidate with non-zero segments beyond the spec's precision is skipped (`precision`) and others are cut to it: `=1.26` sees 2.3.0 as `2.3`, not 2.3.4.

**Version specs (`rangeStrategy`).**

- The dep's version is the spec's anchor: the first clause that is not `<`, `<=` or `!=`, else the first upper bound.
- Matching follows conda's VersionSpec: clauses joined by `,` must all hold; `=1.26`, `1.26.*` and `1.26*` match the versions whose segments start with 1.26 (1.26, 1.26.0, 1.26.4, not 1.260); a bare version or `==` matches exactly (`1.26` = `1.26.0`); `~=1.4.5` is `>=1.4.5,1.4.*`.
- There is no lockfile, so under `auto` (`update-lockfile`) and `replace` versions the spec admits are not proposed: `numpy>=1.26` never gets an update, `numpy=1.26` only once 1.27 is out.
- Rewrites: an exact spec (`==1.26.4`, `1.26.4`) or a fuzzy one (`=1.26`, `1.26.*`) takes the new version, a fuzzy one at its own precision (`=1.26` → `=2.3`); any other spec is rewritten with the pep440 rules of the Python managers (`>=1.26,<2` → `>=2.3,<3`), as Renovate's conda versioning delegates to pep440, when its versions are PEP 440 versions, else the update is not proposed. `pin` writes `==<version>`.

**pip requirements.**

- The `pip:` list holds requirements as a requirements file does: they are updated like `pip_requirements` deps (PyPI, `pep440`, the specifier rules of the Python managers) and get PyPI security updates from OSV.
- `--index-url`/`-i` and `--extra-index-url` entries of the list set the index of its requirements; other options (`-r requirements.txt`, `-e .`, `-c`) are no deps.
- The `python` spec of `dependencies` (`python=3.11` → `==3.11.*`) is the requirements' Python constraint: releases that do not support it are dropped (see the `pypi` datasource).

## terraform

Updates provider, module and Terraform version constraints in Terraform and OpenTofu configurations, then refreshes `.terraform.lock.hcl`. HCL files are read with a small scanner that understands the whole syntax (strings, templates, heredocs, comments, nested expressions) but only interprets literal strings and object constructors; JSON configuration ([JSON syntax](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/syntax/json), e.g. CDK for Terraform's `cdk.tf.json`) is read into the same structure, so it gives the same deps.

**Files:**

- `*.tf`, `*.tofu`, `*.tf.json`, `*.tofu.json` (not below a `.terraform` data directory)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `required_provider` | `terraform { required_providers { <name> = { source, version } } }`; a bare `<name> = "<constraint>"` means `hashicorp/<name>` | `terraform-provider` | `hashicorp` | updated |
| `provider` | the legacy `version` of a `provider "<name>"` block; the source is the file's `required_providers` entry of that name, else `hashicorp/<name>`. Blocks without `version` are not deps. | `terraform-provider` | `hashicorp` | updated |
| `module` | `module` blocks: a registry `source` (`[host/]namespace/name/provider[//subdir]`) with its `version`, or a git `source` with `?ref=` | registry: `terraform-module`; git: `git-tags` | registry: `hashicorp`; git: `semver`, partial refs `tag` | updated |
| `required_version` | `terraform { required_version }` | `github-releases` (`hashicorp/terraform`; `opentofu/opentofu` in `*.tofu` files) | `hashicorp` | updated |
| `helm_release` | `chart`, `repository` and `version` of a `helm_release` resource (also `chart = "oci://host/path/name"`); only exact versions are rewritten, as with the helm manager | `helm` | `semver` | updated |
| `tfe_workspace` | `terraform_version` of a `tfe_workspace` resource | `github-releases` (`hashicorp/terraform`) | `hashicorp` | updated |
| `docker_image` | `name` of a `docker_image` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `docker_container` | `image` of a `docker_container` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `docker_service` | `task_spec { container_spec { image } }` of a `docker_service` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `docker_registry_image` | `name` of a `docker_registry_image` data source | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_pod` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_pod` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_pod_v1` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_pod_v1` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_deployment` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_deployment` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_deployment_v1` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_deployment_v1` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_daemonset` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_daemonset` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_daemon_set_v1` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_daemon_set_v1` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_stateful_set` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_stateful_set` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_stateful_set_v1` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_stateful_set_v1` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_job` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_job` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_job_v1` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_job_v1` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_cron_job` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_cron_job` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_cron_job_v1` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_cron_job_v1` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_replication_controller` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_replication_controller` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `kubernetes_replication_controller_v1` | `image` of every `container` / `init_container` block of a `kubernetes_replication_controller_v1` resource | `docker` | `docker` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unsupported constraint` | a value that is not `[op] <version>`, e.g. empty |
| `no version constraint` | a provider or registry module without `version` |
| `non-literal value` | a version or provider entry that is an expression (`var.v`, `"${…}"`) |
| `non-literal source` | a `source` that is an expression |
| `cannot locate value` | a value with escapes, or a URL-encoded `ref` |
