- `elm.json` at any depth; its `type` (`application` or `package`) decides how it is read, other files have no deps

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `direct` | application `dependencies.direct` (`"elm/json": "1.1.3"`) | `elm-package` | `semver` | updated |
| `indirect` | application `dependencies.indirect`; ignored by default (`ignore: false` opts in) | `elm-package` | `semver` | ignored (opt in with a rule setting `ignore: false`) |
| `test-direct` | application `test-dependencies.direct` | `elm-package` | `semver` | updated |
| `test-indirect` | application `test-dependencies.indirect`; ignored by default (`ignore: false` opts in) | `elm-package` | `semver` | ignored (opt in with a rule setting `ignore: false`) |
| `dependencies` | package `dependencies` constraints (`"elm/core": "1.0.0 <= v < 2.0.0"`) | `elm-package` | `semver`; the constraint is the dep's range, its lower bound the current version | updated |
| `test-dependencies` | package `test-dependencies` constraints | `elm-package` | `semver`, as `dependencies` | updated |
| `elm-version` | `elm-version`: the compiler version of an application (`0.19.1`), the compiler constraint of a package (`0.19.0 <= v < 0.20.0`); the name is `elm/compiler` | `github-releases` (`elm/compiler`) | `semver` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `invalid package name` | a dependency name that is not `author/project` |
| `unsupported version` | an application version that is not `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, or a value with JSON escapes |
| `unsupported constraint` | a package constraint outside Elm's `<lower> <op> v <op> <upper>` grammar (`<` or `<=`, `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` bounds) |

**Applications.**

- Every version is exact and replaced by the new one. The `indirect` versions pin the dependencies of the `direct` ones, which `elm make` checks against their constraints: they are ignored by default, as Go's indirect requirements, and a direct update whose new version needs newer indirect dependencies fails `elm make` until they are raised (`elm install` does that).

**Package constraints.**

- `rangeStrategy` applies to package constraints (`dependencies`, `test-dependencies`, `elm-version`). Packages have no lockfile, so versions a constraint admits are not proposed except under `bump`.
- `auto` (default) is `widen`, Dependabot's update of Elm packages: the lower bound stays and an upper bound the new version reaches moves past it (`1.0.0 <= v < 2.0.0` → `1.0.0 <= v < 3.0.0` for 2.1.0).
- `replace` and `update-lockfile` also set the lower bound to the new version (`2.1.0 <= v < 3.0.0`); `bump` does so for admitted versions too (`1.0.0 <= v < 2.0.0` → `1.2.0 <= v < 2.0.0`). An exclusive upper bound moves to the next boundary of its precision above the new version (`< 2.0.0` → `< 3.0.0`, `< 1.5.0` → `< 1.8.0` for 1.7.2), an inclusive one to the new version. `pin` writes `2.1.0 <= v <= 2.1.0`.

## composer

Updates the version constraints of PHP packages in `composer.json` and moves `composer.lock` with `composer update` (in-range updates only touch the lock, as Renovate's `update-lockfile`). composer.json is read as JSON; only the constraint strings that change are rewritten, so formatting and key order are kept.

**Files:**

- `composer.json` (its lock: the `composer.lock` next to it)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `require` | entries of `require`: `"vendor/package": "<constraint>"` (updates use commit type `fix`) | `packagist` (Packagist, or the `repositories` of type composer), `git-tags` for a package of a vcs repository keyed by its name | `composer` | updated |
| `require-dev` | entries of `require-dev` | `packagist` (Packagist, or the `repositories` of type composer), `git-tags` for a package of a vcs repository keyed by its name | `composer` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `platform package` | a platform package, any name without a vendor: `php`, `ext-*`, `lib-*`, `composer`, `composer-plugin-api`, `composer-runtime-api` |
| `unsupported constraint` | a constraint outside Composer's grammar for tagged versions: branches (`dev-main`, `2.x-dev`, `dev-main#abc123`), aliases (`dev-main as 1.0.0`), `self.version`, a bare stability flag (`@dev`) |
| `cannot locate value` | a constraint written with JSON escapes (`\u003e=1.0`) |
| `path repository` | a package of a `path` repository: keyed by its name in `repositories`, or installed from one per composer.lock (dist type `path`) |
| `package repository` | a package a `package` repository defines |
| `unsupported repository URL` | a vcs repository keyed by the package name whose URL is not a git URL deps can list tags of |
| `no composer repository` | `"packagist.org": false` and no composer repository whose `only`/`exclude` filters admit the package |
| `no locked version` | a constraint without a lower bound (`*`, `<2.0`) that the composer.lock next to it does not lock to a tagged version (or without composer.lock) |

**Repositories.**

- `repositories` entries (array or object form) of type `composer` are searched in order with their `only`/`exclude` name patterns, then Packagist unless `"packagist.org": false` (or `"packagist": false`) disables it; the first repository that has the package answers, as Composer's canonical repositories do. See the `packagist` row under [Datasources](#datasources) for the repository formats and `COMPOSER_AUTH`.
- A `vcs` (`git`, `github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`) repository keyed by a package name (object form, or with a `name`, as Renovate reads it) makes that package a `git-tags` dep of its URL; vcs repositories without a name are not mapped to packages (Composer reads their composer.json to find out), so their packages are still looked up in the composer repositories.

**Constraints.**

- Composer's constraint grammar (composer/semver): `^1.2.3`, `~1.2`, `>=1.0 <2.0` and `>=1.0,<2.0` (blanks after an operator belong to it: `>= 1.0`), `!=`/`<>`, exact versions (`1.2.3`, `==1.2.3`, `v1.2.3`), wildcards (`1.2.*`, `1.x`, `*`), hyphen ranges (`1.0 - 2.0`), `||` and `|` alternatives, and stability flags (`^2.0@beta`). `^0.3` is `>=0.3 <0.4`; `~1.2` is `>=1.2 <2.0` and `~1.2.3` `>=1.2.3 <1.3`. As with Composer's default `minimum-stability: stable`, a version below stable (`2.0.0-RC1`) only satisfies a constraint that names one of its stability or a lower one, or carries such a flag (`@RC`, `@dev`).
- Constraints are rewritten per [rangeStrategy](configuration.md#rangestrategy) (top level or per rule), after Renovate's composer versioning: an exact version takes the new version as published, keeping a `v` prefix as written (`v1.2.3` → `v1.4.0`); `^`, `~`, `>=` and `>` keep their precision (`^5.2.8` → `^6.0.1`, `~1.2` → `~1.4`; `>` becomes `>=`), except that a two-part `^`/`~` moving to a new major is written `<major>.0` (`^4.1` → `^5.0` for 5.2.0); wildcards keep theirs (`1.2.*` → `1.4.*`); upper bounds move past the new version (`>=1.0 <2.0` → `>=2.3 <3.0` for 2.3.0, `<=2.6` → `<=3.1.4`). Stability flags, `v` prefixes and the separators between comparators stay.
- `auto` is `update-lockfile`, as in Renovate: versions the constraint admits are lockfile-only updates from the version composer.lock locks (`, lockfile` in the report; composer.json is unchanged), others replace the constraint; a constraint with alternatives (`^1.0|^2.0`, `^1 || ^2`) is widened instead (`^1.0|^2.0` → `^1.0|^2.0|^3.0`), and so is it under `bump`. Renovate also widens for `"type": "typo3-cms-extension"`; deps does not (set `rangeStrategy: widen` for such packages). Without composer.lock only versions outside the constraint are proposed.
- `bump` raises the lower bounds of the first alternative admitting a new version (`^1.2` → `^1.4`, `>=1.2 <2.0` → `>=1.4 <2.0`), `in-range-only` only to versions the constraint admits; `widen` moves only the upper bounds of the last alternative (`>=1.0 <2.0` → `>=1.0 <3.0`), or appends the replaced last alternative (`^1.2` → `^1.2 || ^2.0`); `pin` writes the exact version. A constraint without a lower bound (`*`, `<2.0`) only gets lockfile-only updates.
- Versioning `composer` orders versions as Composer does: an optional `v`, up to four numeric parts, then `dev` < `alpha` (`a`) < `beta` (`b`) < `RC` < release < `patch` (`p`, `pl`) with their numbers (`1.0.0-beta2`, `2.0.0-RC.1`, `1.0.0-p1`). Branches (`dev-main`, `2.x-dev`) are not versions. Update types follow the first three parts; versions below stable are only proposed from one.

**Lockfile (`apply`, `run`).**

1. **Lockfile.** The lockfile of a `composer.json` is the `composer.lock` next to it; without one the file is only patched.
2. **Locked versions.** Before resolution each composer.lock is read: a package gets the version of its entry in `packages` or `packages-dev` (a branch such as `dev-main` counts as none). An unreadable lock is reported once and its packages are bumped.
3. **Temporary copy.** The directory is mirrored to a temp dir: composer.json and composer.lock are copied, every other entry but `vendor` (`auth.json`, path repositories, patches) is symlinked; the directories above it up to the repository top are recreated with their entries symlinked, so path repositories outside resolve as in the checkout.
4. **Update.** `composer update <name>:<version>… --with-dependencies --minimal-changes` moves every updated package, lockfile-only updates included, to exactly the update's version (the inline constraint keeps Composer from locking a newer one the rewritten constraint admits, e.g. when `minimumReleaseAge` held it back), and its dependencies only where the new version needs it. Every run passes `--no-install --no-scripts --no-plugins --no-audit --no-interaction`: only composer.lock is written. Platform requirements are ignored (`--ignore-platform-reqs`), since the runner's PHP and extensions are not the project's; with a `config.platform.php` in composer.json only extensions and libraries are (`--ignore-platform-req=ext-* --ignore-platform-req=lib-*`), and the PHP requirements are checked against that version. The lock's `content-hash` is recomputed.
5. **Tool.** `composer` (2.7 or later, for `--minimal-changes`) must be on `PATH`, e.g. from `shivammathur/setup-php`; it runs with `COMPOSER` set to the copy, and `COMPOSER_AUTH` and `COMPOSER_HOME` in effect. Without it, the composer.json files fail with `composer not found (needed to update composer.lock)`.
6. **Failure.** A failed command reports `composer update in <dir>: <last 20 output lines>`, and the composer.json's changes are dropped.

- `plan` does not run Composer, and prints `note    composer.lock changes are computed by apply/run`.

**Lock file maintenance (`run`).**

With [lockFileMaintenance](configuration.md#lockfilemaintenance) enabled, every `composer.lock` next to a scanned `composer.json` is refreshed with `composer update` (same options as below) in the temporary copy, which moves every locked package, transitive ones included, to the newest version the constraints admit. All lockfiles share the PR on `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance`, which changes only `composer.lock` files; `minimumReleaseAge` does not apply to it.

## julia

Updates the `[compat]` entries of Julia projects (`Project.toml`, `JuliaProject.toml`) from the General registry, and moves their `Manifest.toml` with Pkg (in-range updates only touch the manifest, as `update-lockfile`). Dependabot's `julia` ecosystem; Renovate has no Julia manager. Only the compat string is rewritten, so the file's layout and comments are kept.

**Files:**

- `Project.toml`, `JuliaProject.toml` (Pkg prefers the latter where both exist; both are read)
- `Manifest.toml`, `JuliaManifest.toml`, `Manifest-v<major>.<minor>.toml` (the locked versions, see below)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deps` | `[compat]` entries of packages in `[deps]` (`JSON = "0.21, 1"`), and `[deps]` packages without a compat entry, which only the manifest moves (updates use commit type `fix`) | `julia-registry` (the General registry) | `julia` | updated |
| `weakdeps` | `[compat]` entries of `[weakdeps]` packages (package extension triggers) | `julia-registry` (the General registry) | `julia` | updated |
| `extras` | `[compat]` entries of `[extras]` packages (test dependencies of `[targets]`) | `julia-registry` (the General registry) | `julia` | updated |
| `julia` | the `julia` compat entry (skipped) | none | `julia` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `julia compat is the project's supported Julia versions` | the `julia` compat entry: which Julia releases a project supports is its authors' decision, not an update |
| `julia standard library` | a standard library (`LinearAlgebra`, `Test`, `Pkg`, the bundled `_jll`s, by UUID): its version is Julia's. Registered former stdlibs (`Statistics`, `DelimitedFiles`) are looked up like any package; stdlibs in `[deps]` without a compat entry are not listed at all |
| `not in [deps], [weakdeps] or [extras]` | a compat entry naming a package the project does not list (Pkg rejects such a project) |
| `compat entry is not a string` | a compat value that is not a string |
| `compat entry with escapes` | a compat string with escapes, whose bytes deps would not rewrite faithfully |
| `unsupported compat entry` | a compat entry outside Pkg's grammar (`> 1`, `<= 2`, `1.x`, `*`, an empty string) |
| `path source` | a package that `[sources]` installs from a `path` |
| `url source` | a package that `[sources]` installs from a git `url` |
| `no Manifest.toml version for a package without a lower bound` | a compat entry with only upper bounds (`< 2`), or a `[deps]` package without a compat entry, that the manifest does not lock (or that has no manifest) |

**Compat entries.**

- Pkg's grammar (`semver_spec`): comma-separated terms, any of which admits a version. A bare or `^` version is a caret range (`1.2.3` = [1.2.3, 2), `0.2.3` = [0.2.3, 0.3), `0.0.3` only 0.0.3, `1` = [1, 2), `0` = [0, 1), `0.0` = [0, 0.1)); `~1.2.3` and `~1.2` are [1.2.x, 1.3), `~1` is [1, 2); `=1.2` is exactly 1.2.0; `>= 1.2` (or `≥`) has no upper bound, `< 1.2` no lower one; `1.2 - 2` is [1.2, 3). A `v` prefix is allowed. Prereleases and builds count as their release.
- Versioning `julia` orders versions as Julia's VersionNumber does (1–3 parts, `-pre` and `+build` after three; JLL rebuilds `1.2.11+1` > `1.2.11+0`). Update types follow the caret: the leftmost non-zero part is the major (`0.21` → `0.22` is major, `1.2` → `1.3` minor). Prereleases are only proposed from a prerelease.
- Rewrites per [rangeStrategy](configuration.md#rangestrategy): `widen` appends a term for the new version in the style of the term with the highest upper bound, the new version's caret prefix for caret terms (`0.21, 1` → `0.21, 1, 2` for 2.3.4, `0.21` → `0.21, 0.22` for 0.22.1), as CompatHelper does; `~` terms take the version at their precision, `=` terms the version itself (`=1.2` is exactly 1.2.0), and `< 2` or the upper half of `1.2 - 1.5` is raised in place. `replace` (and an out-of-range version under `update-lockfile` and `bump`) writes that one term with the version at its precision (`0.21, 1` → `2`, `4.2` → `5.1`, `~1.2` → `~1.5`, `=0.3.1` → `=0.4.2`). `bump` and `in-range-only` drop the terms entirely below an admitted version and raise the floor of the term admitting it (`0.21, 1` → `1` for 1.4.5, `1.2` → `1.4`); `pin` writes `=<version>`.
- `auto` is `update-lockfile` for a project with a manifest (an application, or a workspace committing its manifest): versions the compat entry admits are manifest-only updates from the locked version (`, lockfile` in the report), others replace the entry. A project without one (a package: registered packages do not commit manifests) gets `widen`, the Julia convention of keeping older majors supported; versions the entry admits are not proposed then.
- A `[deps]` package without a compat entry admits any version (`>= 0` in reports): it is never written into the project, only moved in the manifest (`update-lockfile`, `bump`, `in-range-only`).
- Each compat entry is looked up by its name and the UUID its `[deps]`, `[weakdeps]` or `[extras]` entry gives; a package the General registry does not have (a private registry's) is skipped with the datasource's reason.

**Manifest (`apply`, `run`).**

1. **Manifest.** A project's manifest is `JuliaManifest.toml` or `Manifest.toml` next to it, else the `Manifest-v<major>.<minor>.toml` of the newest Julia release there (other versioned manifests are neither read nor updated). A project listed in the `[workspace] projects` of a project in a directory above (Julia 1.12 workspaces, nested ones too) uses the manifest of the workspace root; without a manifest the project is only patched.
2. **Locked versions.** Before resolution each manifest (format 1 or 2) is read: a package gets the `version` of its entry with the package's UUID; entries tracking a `path` or a git `repo-url` are not registry versions and are left out. An unreadable manifest is reported once and its packages are bumped.
3. **Temporary copy.** The manifest's directory is mirrored to a temp dir: project files are copied (patched ones with their new compat entries), the manifest is written as `Manifest.toml` (so Pkg reads it whatever its Julia version), other files are symlinked; the directories above it up to the repository top are recreated with their entries symlinked, so `[sources]` paths resolve as in the checkout.
4. **Update.** For each project of the scope with updates, `julia` runs `Pkg.activate(<project>)` and `Pkg.add([Pkg.PackageSpec(name=…, uuid=…, version="<new version>"), …])` for its updated `[deps]` packages the manifest locks, which moves exactly those to the update's version (a build suffix dropped) and keeps every other locked version Pkg can keep. A project whose updates move no locked package (compat entries of `[weakdeps]` and `[extras]`) runs `Pkg.resolve()` instead, which records the new compat entries in the manifest's `project_hash` and moves what they exclude. Lockfile-only updates are added the same way, with the project unchanged. Only the manifest is taken back.
5. **Tool.** `julia` must be on `PATH` (e.g. `julia-actions/setup-julia`); it runs with `JULIA_PKG_PRECOMPILE_AUTO=0` and the runner's depot, installing the General registry first when the depot has none. Pkg installs the packages of the manifest as it resolves (into the depot, not the repository). Without `julia`, the projects fail with `julia not found (needed to update Manifest.toml)`.
6. **Failure.** A failed run reports `julia Pkg in <dir>: <last 20 output lines>`, and the scope's changes are dropped.

- `plan` does not run Julia, and prints `note    Manifest.toml changes are computed by apply/run`.

**Lock file maintenance (`run`).**

With [lockFileMaintenance](configuration.md#lockfilemaintenance) enabled, every manifest of a scanned project (a workspace's once) is refreshed with `Pkg.update()` in the temporary copy, which moves every locked package, transitive ones included, to the newest version the compat entries admit. All manifests share the PR on `<branchPrefix>lock-file-maintenance`, which changes only manifests; `minimumReleaseAge` does not apply to it.

## bazel-module

Updates Bazel module dependencies (bzlmod): `bazel_dep` versions from Bazel registries, git overrides and git repository rules, and the images, Maven artifacts and crates of the rules_oci, rules_img, rules_jvm_external and rules_rust module extensions, as Renovate's bazel-module manager. Files are read with a small Starlark lexer (strings, lists, comments, nested calls and list comprehensions); only the string values that change are rewritten. `MODULE.bazel.lock` is regenerated with `bazel mod deps`.

**Files:**

- `MODULE.bazel` and the segments it includes (`<name>.MODULE.bazel`, Renovate's `(^|/|\.)MODULE\.bazel$`)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bazel_dep` | `bazel_dep(name = …, version = …)` (also with `repo_name`, `dev_dependency`, `max_compatibility_level`) | `bazel` | `bazel-module` | updated |
| `single_version_override` | `single_version_override(module_name = …, version = …)`: the pinned version is listed but not updated (Renovate: `ignored`); its `registry` becomes the registry of the module's bazel_dep | `bazel` | `bazel-module` | updated |
| `git_override` | `git_override(module_name = …, remote = …, commit = …)`: a commit tracks the default branch head (digest updates; Renovate's github-tags without a tag), a `tag` (with or without `commit`) the tags. Named after the module; any git host, not only github.com | `git-refs` (commit), `git-tags` (tag) | `tag` | updated |
| `archive_override` | `archive_override(module_name = …)`: listed and skipped | none | none | updated |
| `local_path_override` | `local_path_override(module_name = …)`: listed and skipped | none | none | updated |
| `multiple_version_override` | `multiple_version_override(module_name = …)`: listed and skipped, and its bazel_dep is not updated (the version must stay one of `versions`; beyond Renovate, which updates it) | none | none | updated |
| `git_repository` | `git_repository(remote = …, commit = …\|tag = …)` repo rules of `use_repo_rule("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:git.bzl", "git_repository")`, as git_override; named after the remote's path | `git-refs` (commit), `git-tags` (tag) | `tag` | updated |
| `new_git_repository` | `new_git_repository(…)` repo rules, as git_repository | `git-refs` (commit), `git-tags` (tag) | `tag` | updated |
| `oci_pull` | `oci.pull(image = …, tag = …, digest = …)` of `use_extension("@rules_oci//oci:extensions.bzl", "oci")`: the tag, and the digest when there is one | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `rules_img_pull` | rules_img `pull(registry = …, repository = …, tag = …, digest = …)` of `use_repo_rule("@rules_img//img:pull.bzl", "pull")`; without `registry` the image is on Docker Hub | `docker` | `docker` | updated |
| `maven_install` | `maven.install(artifacts = ["group:artifact[:packaging[:classifier]]:version", …])` and `maven.artifact(group = …, artifact = …, version = …)` of `use_extension("@rules_jvm_external//:extensions.bzl", "maven")`; the repositories are the `repositories` of the installs with the same `name` (default `maven`), else Maven Central | `maven` | `maven` | updated |
| `crate_spec` | `crate.spec(package = …, version = …)` of `use_extension("@rules_rust//crate_universe:extension.bzl", "crate")`: the version is a Cargo requirement, rewritten as the [cargo](#cargo) manager's (`rangeStrategy`; without a lockfile deps reads, versions it admits are not proposed); `git` crates with a `tag` are git-tags deps | `crate` (crates.io), `git-tags` (git with tag) | `cargo`, `tag` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `no version` | a bazel_dep or maven.artifact without `version` or with `version = ""`, a maven.install artifact without one (`group:artifact`, managed by a BOM) |
| `non-literal value` | a name, version, remote, image, tag or digest that is not a plain string literal (a variable, a concatenation, `None`, an escaped string) |
| `pinned by single_version_override` | a bazel_dep whose module has a `single_version_override` with a `version` |
| `overridden by <override>` | a bazel_dep whose module has a `git_override`, `archive_override`, `local_path_override` or `multiple_version_override` (in the same file or in another module file of the workspace) |
| `version override` | the `single_version_override` itself: an override pins a version on purpose (often with `patches`), as in Renovate |
| `archive override` | an `archive_override` |
| `local path override` | a `local_path_override` |
| `multiple versions` | a `multiple_version_override` |
| `unrecognized remote` | a `remote` that is not an https/http/ssh/git or `git@host:path` URL with an owner/repo path |
| `branch reference` | a git override or repository with `branch` and neither `commit` nor `tag` |
| `no commit or tag` | a git override or repository without `commit` (a full 40-character SHA-1), `tag` or `branch` |
| `invalid image` | an image that does not parse, or already carries a tag or digest |
| `digest without tag` | an image with a `digest` but no `tag` |
| `no tag` | an image without `tag` and `digest` |
| `invalid coordinates` | a maven artifact that is not `group:artifact[:packaging[:classifier]]:version` |
| `path dependency` | a crate.spec with `path` |
| `git dependency` | a crate.spec with `git` and no `tag` (a `branch` or `rev`), or an unrecognized git URL |
| `unsupported requirement` | a crate.spec version outside the Cargo requirement forms of the cargo manager |

**Modules and overrides.**

- Only Bazel's module file functions and the extension tags and repo rules above are read; `module()`, `use_repo`, `include` and other extensions are ignored. Extension variables are recognized by their `use_extension`/`use_repo_rule` call in the same file (included segments cannot share variables), not by their name.
- Overrides apply to the bazel_dep of their `module_name` in every module file of the workspace: the files whose nearest directory holding a scanned `MODULE.bazel` is the same (the root module and its `*.MODULE.bazel` segments). A module with more than one override (an error in Bazel) keeps its bazel_dep updatable.
- Module versions are looked up in the workspace's registries: the `--registry` flags of the `.bazelrc` next to the `MODULE.bazel`, else the Bazel Central Registry; a `single_version_override(registry = …)` replaces them for its module. See the `bazel` datasource in [Datasources](#datasources).
- Versioning `bazel-module` orders versions as Bazel does: `RELEASE[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]` with dot-separated identifiers, digit-only ones numerically and before the others (`1.2.3` < `1.2.3.1` < `1.2.3.bcr.1` < `1.2.4`; registry patches such as `1.8.2.bcr.1` are patch updates), a prerelease below its release, build metadata ignored. Update types follow the first three release identifiers. Prereleases (`1.5.6-9.bcr.2`, `2025-11-05.bcr.1`, whose release is `2025`) are only proposed from a prerelease.

**MODULE.bazel.lock.**

- With an update of a module file whose workspace has a `MODULE.bazel.lock`, `apply` and `run` run `bazel --output_base=<tmp> mod deps --lockfile_mode=update` (`bazelisk` when `bazel` is not on `PATH`; Bazelisk uses the workspace's `.bazelversion`) in a temporary mirror of the workspace with the patched module files (other entries symlinked, so patches, `local_path_override` paths and `.bazelrc` resolve), then `bazel shutdown`. The new lockfile joins the update; a workspace without one gets none.
- Without Bazel the update fails with `bazel not found (needed to update MODULE.bazel.lock)`; `plan` does not run Bazel and notes `note    MODULE.bazel.lock changes are computed by apply/run`.
- `lockFileMaintenance` deletes and regenerates every `MODULE.bazel.lock` next to a scanned `MODULE.bazel` the same way, as Renovate does. `.bazelversion` updates (the [bazelisk](#bazelisk) manager) do not regenerate it.

## bazelisk

Updates the Bazel version Bazelisk reads from `.bazelversion` (its first line), as Renovate's bazelisk manager.

**Files:**

- `.bazelversion` at any depth

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bazel` | the Bazel version (name `bazelbuild/bazel`) | `github-releases` (`bazelbuild/bazel`) | `semver` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `bazel fork` | `<fork>/<version>` (a Bazel fork Bazelisk downloads from another GitHub repository) |
| `non-release version` | `latest`, `latest-<n>`, `last_green`, `last_rc`, `7.x`, `*`: Bazelisk resolves them itself |

## nuget

Updates NuGet package references, MSBuild project SDKs and .NET tools in MSBuild files, central package management (`Directory.Packages.props`), `global.json` (also the .NET SDK) and `dotnet-tools.json`. MSBuild files are scanned with encoding/xml at byte offsets and only the version is rewritten, so attribute order, quotes, comments, whitespace and a UTF-8 byte order mark are kept. NuGet is not run; `packages.lock.json` files are not updated.

**Files:**

- `*.csproj`, `*.fsproj`, `*.vbproj` and MSBuild imports `*.props`, `*.targets` (`Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Build.targets`, `Directory.Packages.props`, any other; not the `*.nuget.g.props`/`*.nuget.g.targets` restore generates). A file whose root element is not `<Project>` yields no deps
- `global.json` (comments allowed, as the .NET SDK reads it)
- `dotnet-tools.json` (the local tool manifest, usually `.config/dotnet-tools.json`)
- `nuget.config` (any case: `NuGet.Config`, `NuGet.config`): package sources only, no deps

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nuget` | `PackageReference`, `PackageVersion` (central package management), `GlobalPackageReference`, `PackageDownload` and `DotNetCliToolReference` items in an `<ItemGroup>` (conditions included) with `Include` or `Update` and a `Version` (or `VersionOverride`, which wins) attribute or child element; dotnet-tools.json `tools.<id>.version` | `nuget` (nuget.org, or the nuget.config package sources) | `nuget` | updated |
| `msbuild-sdk` | `<Project Sdk="Microsoft.Build.NoTargets/3.7.134">` (each `;`-separated `Name/Version`), `<Sdk Name="…" Version="…" />`, `<Import Project="…" Sdk="…" Version="…" />`, global.json `msbuild-sdks` entries; SDKs without a version ship with the .NET SDK and are not deps | `nuget` (nuget.org, or the nuget.config package sources) | `nuget` | updated |
| `dotnet-sdk` | global.json `sdk.version` (name `dotnet-sdk`); `rollForward` is kept | `dotnet-version` | `nuget` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `no version` | an empty version (`Version=""`) |
| `invalid version "<v>"` | a version outside NuGet's version and range grammar (`latest`, `1.0-*-*`, a floating bound inside an interval) |
| `floating version <v>` | `*` or `*-*`: every version is admitted, so there is nothing to update |
| `non-literal version <v>` | a version that combines properties or text (`$(Major).1.0`, `$(A)$(B)`) |
| `undefined property $(<name>)` | a `$(Name)` version no unconditional `<PropertyGroup>` of the file, of a `Directory.Packages.props` or of a `Directory.Build.props` above it defines |
| `property cycle $(<name>)` | a chain of property references deeper than 8 |
| `cannot locate value` | a version written with XML entities, CDATA or a comment inside the element |
| `non-literal package id` | an `Include` that is not one literal package id (`$(Prefix).Core`, `A;B`) |
| `no http(s) package source in nuget.config` | the nuget.config files clear the package sources and add only local folders or `%VAR%` URLs |
| `no packageSourceMapping pattern matches the package` | `packageSourceMapping` is configured and no pattern matches the package id |

**Versions and ranges.**

- Versioning `nuget` is NuGetVersion: one to four numeric parts (missing ones are 0, `1.2` = `1.2.0.0`), a `-` prerelease compared as SemVer 2.0 (case-insensitive), `+metadata` ignored. Update types follow the first two parts (a third or fourth one is a patch). Prereleases are only proposed from a prerelease.
- A bare version (`Version="13.0.3"`, NuGet's minimum version) and an exact range (`[13.0.3]`) are updated as the pinned version they are in practice: the new version replaces the old one (`[13.0.3]` → `[13.0.4]`), as Renovate does.
- Floating versions and intervals are ranges, rewritten per [rangeStrategy](configuration.md#rangestrategy) (`auto` is `update-lockfile`; deps does not read `packages.lock.json`, so versions a range admits are not proposed): a floating version moves at its precision when a version leaves it (`13.*` → `14.*`, `1.2.*` → `1.3.*`, `1.0.0-rc*` → `1.1.0-rc*`); an interval gets a new upper bound, the new version when inclusive, else the next value at the position where the bounds differ (`[1.0,2.0)` → `[1.0,3.0)` for 2.5.1, `(,2.0)` → `(,3.0)`), with its lower bound kept. `bump` raises an interval's lower bound to every newer version it admits (`[1.0,2.0)` → `[1.5.0,2.0)`); `pin` writes the bare version. `*` and `*-*` are skipped.

**Properties.**

- A version written as `$(Name)` (`<PackageVersion Include="Serilog" Version="$(SerilogVersion)" />`) is read from the last definition of `<Name>` in an unconditional top-level `<PropertyGroup>` of the file itself, else of the `Directory.Packages.props`, else of the `Directory.Build.props` of its directory, then of each directory above (MSBuild property names are case-insensitive). The update edits the definition, and deps sharing it are grouped into one PR with one version. Properties inside a `Condition`, `<Choose>` or `<Target>` are not read.

**Package sources.**

- Packages are looked up on nuget.org unless `nuget.config` files say otherwise: the files of the dep's directory and every directory above it up to the repository root are applied from the root down, as NuGet merges them (nearer files win): `<packageSources>` `<add key value>`, `<remove key>` and `<clear/>` (dropping nuget.org and the sources of files above), `<disabledPackageSources>`, and `<packageSourceMapping>`, under which a package is looked up only on the sources whose patterns hold its most specific match (an exact id over the longest `Prefix.*`, `*` last). The machine and user configurations of the runner are not read.
- Local folder sources (`./packages`, `C:\feed`) and URLs with `%VAR%` references are left out. The versions of all remaining sources are merged, as NuGet restores from all of them; v2 feeds (`…/api/v2`) are not read. Credentials come from `NuGetPackageSourceCredentials_<key>` (see [Datasources](#datasources)).

**global.json and dotnet-tools.json.**

- global.json's `sdk.version` is the .NET SDK (`dotnet-sdk`, datasource `dotnet-version`): updates move it to a newer SDK, feature bands included (`8.0.100` → `8.0.404`, a patch), and to newer majors as major updates; previews only from a preview. Its `msbuild-sdks` (`"Microsoft.Build.Traversal": "4.1.0"`) are NuGet packages of dep type `msbuild-sdk`.
- dotnet-tools.json `tools.<id>.version` entries are NuGet packages of dep type `nuget` (`dotnet-ef`, `csharpier`); the `commands` are kept.

## ansible-galaxy

Updates the roles and collections of Ansible Galaxy requirements files and the collection dependencies of `galaxy.yml`.

**Files:**

- `requirements.yml`, `requirements.yaml`, `requirements.ansible.yml` (`.yaml`) at any depth: `roles` and `collections` lists, or a top-level list of roles (the old format)
- `galaxy.yml`, `galaxy.yaml`, `galaxy.ansible.yml` (`.yaml`) at any depth: the collection's `dependencies` mapping

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `role` | `roles[]` entry: `src` (else `name`) and `version`, or a `src,version` string. A Galaxy role `namespace.name`, or an SCM URL (`git+https://…`, `https://…`, `git@host:owner/repo`; `scm: git`) | `galaxy` (`namespace.name`), `git-tags` (SCM URLs: the name is the URL path `owner/repo`, the source its `https://` URL) | `tag` | updated |
| `galaxy-collection` | `collections[]` entry: `name` and `version` (a bare version, `==`, or a range such as `>=1.0.0,<2.0.0`), the Galaxy server of `source`, or `type: git` with the repository URL as name (`git+https://…/repo.git,v1.0.0`); galaxy.yml `dependencies` (`community.general: ">=8.0.0"`, or an SCM URL key with a git version: `'git+https://github.com/o/r': v1.0.0`) | `galaxy-collection` (`namespace.name`, the source the entry's `source`), `git-tags` (`type: git` and SCM URL names) | `pep440` (Galaxy), `tag` (git) | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `no version` | an entry without `version` (or `,version`), an empty or non-string specifier |
| `unconstrained` | a collection specifier `*` or only `!=` exclusions |
| `unsupported range` | a collection specifier that is not a PEP 440 specifier set |
| `non-version ref` | a role or git version that is not a version tag (a branch, a commit) |
| `no name` | a collection entry without `name`, a name or galaxy.yml key that is neither `namespace.name` nor an SCM URL |
| `local source` | a local path, `type: file`, `dir` or `subdirs` |
| `unsupported source` | a tarball URL (`type: url`), `scm: hg`, a role name that is not `namespace.name`, or an SCM URL without an `owner/repo` path |
| `cannot locate value` | the version bytes were not found (escapes, block scalars) |

**Details.**

- The role and git versions are replaced in place, keeping quotes and comments; versions cannot be pinned to digests.
- Collection specifiers are PEP 440 specifier sets in which a bare version means `==` (ansible-galaxy's syntax): their version is the range's anchor and they are rewritten per `rangeStrategy` like Python specifiers (`auto` = `update-lockfile`: a bare or `==` version is replaced by the new version, an open range such as `>=8.0.0` only moves for a version outside it).
- `include:` entries of requirements files are not followed (the included file is extracted on its own when its name matches). List entries with keys other than `src`, `name`, `role`, `version` and `scm` are not roles (a task file named `requirements.yml`).

## ansible

Updates container images in Ansible task files.

**Files:**

- `tasks/*.yml` / `tasks/*.yaml` at any depth (a role's `tasks/main.yml`)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | every scalar `image` value of the task file, at any depth (`community.docker.docker_container`, `containers.podman.podman_container`, …) | `docker` | `docker` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `template` | a Jinja2 expression (`{{`) in the image |
| `variable reference` | `$` in the image |
| `invalid reference` | the image reference does not parse |
| `no tag` | an image without tag |
| `digest without tag` | an image pinned by digest only |
| `cannot locate value` | the value bytes were not found (escapes, block scalars) |

**Details.**

- Images are parsed and edited like the docker manager: tags update, digests are refreshed or pinned.
- Files without `image` are not parsed.

## sbt

Updates sbt builds as Renovate's sbt manager: library and plugin ModuleIDs of `*.sbt` and `project/*.scala` files, `scalaVersion`, and `sbt.version` of `project/build.properties`. Files are read with a small Scala lexer (strings, comments, objects, `val`s); versions are rewritten where they are written, also when a `val` in another file of the build defines them.

**Files:**

- `*.sbt` at any depth
- `project/*.scala`
- `project/build.properties`
- `repositories` at the root (sbt's proxy repositories file)

| Dep type | Extracted | Datasource | Versioning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `compile` | ModuleIDs `"group" % "artifact" % "version"` (`%%`/`%%%` append the build's Scala binary version to the artifact: `cats-core_2.13`) anywhere in a file (`libraryDependencies += …`, `Seq(…)`, `val x = …`), whose `% <configuration>` is absent or not one below (`Compile`, `"compile"`, custom configurations) | `sbt-package` | `maven` | updated |
| `test` | ModuleIDs `"group" % "artifact" % "version"` (`%%`/`%%%` append the build's Scala binary version to the artifact: `cats-core_2.13`) anywhere in a file (`libraryDependencies += …`, `Seq(…)`, `val x = …`), whose `% <configuration>` is `Test`/`"test"` (the first configuration of `"test->test"`, `"test;provided"`) | `sbt-package` | `maven` | updated |
| `provided` | ModuleIDs `"group" % "artifact" % "version"` (`%%`/`%%%` append the build's Scala binary version to the artifact: `cats-core_2.13`) anywhere in a file (`libraryDependencies += …`, `Seq(…)`, `val x = …`), whose `% <configuration>` is `Provided`/`"provided"` | `sbt-package` | `maven` | updated |
| `runtime` | ModuleIDs `"group" % "artifact" % "version"` (`%%`/`%%%` append the build's Scala binary version to the artifact: `cats-core_2.13`) anywhere in a file (`libraryDependencies += …`, `Seq(…)`, `val x = …`), whose `% <configuration>` is `Runtime`/`"runtime"` | `sbt-package` | `maven` | updated |
| `optional` | ModuleIDs `"group" % "artifact" % "version"` (`%%`/`%%%` append the build's Scala binary version to the artifact: `cats-core_2.13`) anywhere in a file (`libraryDependencies += …`, `Seq(…)`, `val x = …`), whose `% <configuration>` is `Optional`/`"optional"` | `sbt-package` | `maven` | updated |
| `it` | ModuleIDs `"group" % "artifact" % "version"` (`%%`/`%%%` append the build's Scala binary version to the artifact: `cats-core_2.13`) anywhere in a file (`libraryDependencies += …`, `Seq(…)`, `val x = …`), whose `% <configuration>` is `IntegrationTest`/`"it"` | `sbt-package` | `maven` | updated |
| `plugin` | `addSbtPlugin("group" % "artifact" % "version")` (named `group:artifact`, looked up for the build's sbt version), and compiler plugins `addCompilerPlugin(…)`/`compilerPlugin(…)` (cross-versioned as libraries) | `sbt-plugin` (addSbtPlugin), `sbt-package` (compiler plugins) | `maven` | updated |
| `scala` | `scalaVersion := "2.13.16"` (also `ThisBuild / scalaVersion`, `scalaVersion in ThisBuild`, a `val`, `<seq>.head`): `org.scala-lang:scala-library`, `org.scala-lang:scala3-library_3` for Scala 3 | `maven` | `maven` | updated |
| `sbt` | `sbt.version` of `project/build.properties` (name `sbt/sbt`) | `github-releases` (`sbt/sbt`) | `semver` | updated |

**Skips:**

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `non-literal version` | a version that is an expression (`sys.props.getOrElse(…)`, `(v + ".0")`), an interpolated or escaped string |
| `unresolved version <ref>` | a version reference no `val` of the build defines as a string literal (`scalaVersion.value`, a setting key) |
| `dynamic version` | an Ivy dynamic revision: `latest.integration`, `1.+`, `[1.0,2.0)` |
| `unresolved Scala version` | a `%%`/`%%%` (or `CrossVersion.full`) ModuleID of a build whose `scalaVersion` and `crossScalaVersions` settings do not resolve to a literal |
| `unresolved group or artifact` | only when a file is extracted alone: a ModuleID whose group or artifact refers to a `val` of another file; with the whole build, ModuleIDs whose group or artifact is not a string are not deps |

**Builds and definitions.**

- A build is a directory with a `project/` directory (else the directory of a `*.sbt` file): its `*.sbt` files and those of subdirectories, `project/*.scala`, `project/*.sbt` and `project/build.properties`.
- Versions, groups and artifacts may be `val`/`lazy val`/`var`/parameterless `def` references, also qualified by objects (`Dependencies.Versions.cats`, `V.cats` for an anonymous `val V = new { val cats = … }`) and across the files of a build; `val a = b` chains, `<module>.revision` (the version of another ModuleID `val`) and `<seq>.head` are followed. The update edits the definition; deps sharing it are grouped into one PR.
- The Scala binary version of `%%` is that of the first `scalaVersion` that resolves to a literal (`*.sbt` at the build root first, then `project/*.scala`, then other `*.sbt`), else of the first element of `crossScalaVersions`; without either setting sbt's default (Scala 2.12 for sbt 1.x, Scala 3 for sbt 2.x). `.cross(CrossVersion.full)` appends the full Scala version, `for3Use2_13` and `for2_13Use3` swap 3 and 2.13, `disabled` none. Deps of `project/*.sbt` (the meta-build) use sbt's own Scala version.
- Scala releases are compared with the `maven` versioning; Scala 3.8+ is also published as `scala-library`, so a Scala 2 project sees it as a major update (as in Renovate); a rule `{names: [org.scala-lang:scala-library], updates: [minor, patch]}` keeps Scala 2.

**Repositories.**

- Libraries are looked up in Maven Central, then the `resolvers += "name" at "url"` (also `++= Seq(…)`) of the build's files; `project/*.sbt` resolvers apply to the meta-build's deps.
- Plugins are looked up in the sbt plugin releases repository (Ivy layout) and Maven Central, then the meta-build's resolvers. A root `repositories` file (sbt's `[repositories]` proxies: `maven-central`, `name: url[, ivy pattern]`) replaces these defaults for every build; entries with an `[organization]` pattern are Ivy repositories.
- `scalaVersion` deps use the library repositories with the `maven` datasource.
